articles.headline: Iranian negotiators continue talks in Doha to end U.S.-Iran war
articles.title: Iranian negotiators in Doha to continue talks to end the U.S.-Iran war, official says
articles.summary: Iranian delegates met with Qatari mediators in Doha on November 1, 2026, for a third consecutive day of discussions to end the ongoing conflict. According to an official, the talks are coordinated with Washington as officials navigate diplomatic efforts amidst concerns of regional escalation following upcoming U.S. midterm elections, while Tehran's military remains on high alert.
articles.description: The talks come amid concerns that the conflict ‌could escalate again after the November 3 U.S. midterm elections

articles.headline: Binance restores customer withdrawals following record cryptocurrency theft
articles.title: Binance restarts withdrawals after $6.3bn heist
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance resumed withdrawals in stages on Sunday after hackers stole approximately 6.3 billion dollars in digital assets last week. The company stated it has replaced about 95 percent of the affected funds and will absorb the financial loss. Meanwhile, the Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed the security breach to North Korea.
articles.description: The FBI says hackers from North Korea are responsible for the theft.

articles.headline: Israeli strike kills Palestinian schoolboy in Deir el-Balah
articles.title: Education under fire: Gaza’s children face death on their way to school
articles.summary: Fourteen-year-old Mohammed Hamad was killed by an Israeli strike on October 17 while walking home from school in the al-Baraka neighbourhood of Deir el-Balah with his younger brother Abdullah. According to the Gaza Ministry of Health, escalating violence near the Yellow Line has resulted in numerous child casualties and school disruptions, leaving surviving students like injured fourth-grader Suad Abd Rabbo in urgent need of overseas medical treatment.
articles.description: Children have faced Israeli bombs and sniper fire since the academic year resumed in Gaza.

articles.headline: German cost-of-living protests turn violent with looting and arrests
articles.title: Peaceful protests in Germany spiral into violence and looting
articles.summary: Demonstrations across Germany regarding living costs escalated into violence and looting in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne, and Hamburg. German authorities confirmed that at least 54 people faced arrest and more than 100 police officers sustained injuries during the unrest. The protests were initially organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt before deteriorating into widespread civil disorder.
articles.description: Thousands joined largely orderly demonstrations earlier in the day, before violence erupted in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg.

articles.headline: US Senator Dan Sullivan vows to accept election outcome
articles.title: Sullivan vows to honour Alaska race outcome, US judge dismisses DOJ lawsuit
articles.summary: Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan promised to respect the upcoming November 3 midterm election results in Alaska. A federal judge dismissed a Department of Justice lawsuit seeking to decertify the race over a spoiler candidate controversy. Sullivan accused his Democratic opponent Mary Peltola of cheating, while Peltola denied any campaign involvement in recruiting the independent candidate.
articles.description: Senator Sullivan's pledge contrasts with the Trump administration's effort to challenge Alaska's election certification.

articles.headline: Israel establishes diplomatic ties with Somaliland through ambassador exchange
articles.title: Israel’s first ambassador to Somaliland presents credentials in Hargeisa
articles.summary: Israel’s first ambassador to Somaliland, Michael Lotem, presented his credentials to President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi in Hargeisa following a diplomatic agreement reached on December 26, 2025. Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991. Somalia President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud challenged the move, alleging Israel seeks access to the Red Sea. The recognition was condemned by Somalia, the Arab League, the African Union, and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation.
articles.description: Israel expands ties with the breakaway territory as Somalia challenges its motives and war intensifies in Yemen.

articles.headline: Israeli forces maintain military siege on Hebron for tenth day
articles.title: Hebron siege continues for 10th day as Israel threatens wider offensive
articles.summary: Israeli forces are maintaining their lockdown on Hebron in the occupied West Bank for the tenth consecutive day following an October 23 attack that killed two Israeli soldiers. According to Mayor Yousef al-Jabari, the siege has displaced over 3,300 Palestinians, caused daily economic losses exceeding 3.8 million dollars, and resulted in infrastructure damage. Meanwhile, the United Nations human rights office reported that Israeli settlers carried out 397 attacks across the territory in October.
articles.description: Hebron's economic losses surpass $3.8m as Israeli forces demolish West Bank homes and close hundreds of businesses.

articles.headline: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva stages political turnaround in Brazil election
articles.title: Historic win, humongous challenges
articles.summary: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva staged a remarkable political turnaround after trailing Flavio Bolsonaro by 45.2 to 47 percent at the end of the first round of Brazil presidential elections, which saw an abstention rate of 21 percent. Thousands of students and workers subsequently marched across urban centers like Niteroi and Rio de Janeiro in widespread protests against Bolsonarism, marking the return of the Left to the streets after more than a decade.
articles.description: Lula tweaked his campaign’s message, speaking more about reducing working hours, relief for indebted families and higher welfare payments under the Bolsa Familia scheme

articles.headline: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight people including one child
articles.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
articles.summary: At least eight people, including a child, were killed in Israeli air strikes across Gaza on November 1, 2026, hospital officials reported. A strike in Gaza City hit civilians near a school, while another in Khan Younis targeted police officers. The attacks occurred despite a year-old ceasefire agreement mediated internationally.
articles.description: Five officers from the Hamas-run police have been killed in Khan Younis and three people, including a child, killed in Gaza City, officials say.

articles.headline: US approves possible sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
articles.title: US greenlights $2.1bn Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
articles.summary: The United States State Department announced the approval of a potential 2.1 billion dollar sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles and related support to Ukraine. According to officials, the interceptors are not expected to be delivered until the early 2030s. Kyiv will fund the purchase using contributions from Canada, Germany, and Norway, alongside European Union loan funds, while Lockheed Martin serves as the principal contractor.
articles.description: Deal would be one of the most significant steps to supply defensive weapons to Kyiv since ​Trump took office in 2025.

articles.headline: Thousands gather at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi for INDIA bloc rally
articles.title: ‘You can break a stick, not a bundle’: Thousands turn up for INDIA bloc rally from across the country
articles.summary: Supporters from across India arrived in Delhi on November 1, 2026, to attend the opposition INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan. Attendees voiced concerns over electoral roll revisions, healthcare, and education. Leaders alleged that authorities attempted to block travel, while participants sought political change and revival ahead of upcoming elections.
articles.description: Citizens, youth groups, farmers and political party workers gather ahead of the Ramlila Maidan rally, saying a united movement is needed to fight alleged vote theft and electoral roll irregularities

articles.headline: Russian authorities report drone strike on Nizhny Novgorod industrial enterprise
articles.title: Russia says drone hit 'industrial enterprise' near Moscow, Kyiv claims hit major refinery
articles.summary: A massive overnight drone attack significantly damaged an industrial plant in the Kstovo district of Nizhny Novgorod, according to regional governor Gleb Nikitin on November 1, 2026. Ukrainian media claimed the target was a major oil refinery. The incident follows recent strikes on Russian energy infrastructure amid ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Gleb Nikitin, governor of Nizhny Novgorod region, reported a "massive drone attack" during the night, during which an "industrial enterprise in the Kstovo district sustained significant damage"

articles.headline: Donald Trump campaigns in Iowa and Kansas to support Republican Senate
articles.title: Trump rallies in Iowa, Kansas to maintain Republican control of US Senate
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump is holding rallies in Iowa and Kansas on November 1, 2026, to help maintain Republican control of the Senate ahead of the midterm elections. The events follow temporary cancellations and come as polls show tight races. Over 52 million Americans have already cast their ballots nationwide.
articles.description: US President Trump returns to the campaign trail after taking a break at his ⁠⁠Mar-a-Lago club in Florida on Saturday.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi warns Prime Minister and Home Minister of future legal action
articles.title: Gyanesh Kumar will go to jail: Rahul Gandhi
articles.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi asserted at an INDIA bloc rally on November 1, 2026, that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah will face legal consequences for alleged electoral irregularities. He also claimed Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar will be jailed for treason, while praising supporters for defending the nation's constitution.
articles.description: At INDIA bloc rally in Ramlila Maidan, LoP says the 2024 mandate for the Modi government was “illegal”; he outlines a post-Narendra Modi vision rooted in inclusivity and harmony

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh coast prepares for landfall of Cyclonic Storm Murasu
articles.title: Days after Cyclone Arnab, Andhra Pradesh braces for Cyclonic Storm Murasu landfall
articles.summary: Five districts in Andhra Pradesh are under a red alert as Cyclonic Storm Murasu approaches for landfall between Nellore and Narsapur on November 2, 2026. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu cancelled a Delhi trip to review safety preparations. The storm follows Cyclone Arnab, which caused severe damage and five deaths.
articles.description: Cyclonic Storm Murasu likely to turn into severe cyclonic storm by Monday morning; red alert issued in five A.P. districts; heavy rain also forecast for parts of Tamil Nadu and Odisha

articles.headline: North Korea tests cluster-bomb warheads in latest military drills
articles.title: North Korea tests cluster-bomb warheads in latest weapons drill
articles.summary: North Korea test-fired cluster-bomb warheads on October 31, 2026, to assess tactical ballistic missile combat adaptation. The official Korean Central News Agency reported that the weapon can devastate a target area of 12 to 13 hectares. This test follows previous trials of attack drones and hypersonic missiles amid rising border tensions involving South Korea.
articles.description: It also came against the backdrop of growing tensions over a landmine explosion along the heavily fortified border between the two Koreas that saw three South Korean soldiers wounded

articles.headline: Iran warns renewed conflict with United States could outlast previous war
articles.title: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threatens strikes
articles.summary: Iran warned on November 1, 2026, that any future military conflict with the United States could surpass past hostilities in duration. Army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia stated that Washington cannot dictate the timing of its conclusion. The warning follows comments from U.S. President Donald Trump regarding potential strikes on remaining targets and recent diplomatic messages.
articles.description: Diplomatic efforts to end the West Asia war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the U.S. and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections

articles.headline: Iran says four tankers on fire after striking mines in Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says four tankers on fire after striking mines in Hormuz
articles.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says four tankers have caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham open to slavery apology without reparations
articles.title: Burnham ‘open’ to UK slavery apology, but not reparations: Why now?
articles.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced openness to apologising for Britain's historical role in the transatlantic slave trade while explicitly rejecting financial reparations. Writing in The Guardian on October 31, 2026, Burnham expressed personal sorrow ahead of a Commonwealth summit in Antigua and Barbuda, contrasting with persistent demands from Caribbean leaders and CARICOM.
articles.description: The UK PM's statement comes as Commonwealth nations meet in Antigua and Barbuda.

articles.headline: India gross GST collections grow 23 percent to over 2.31 lakh crore rupees in October.
articles.title: GST mop-up surges 23% to second-highest level of ₹2.31 lakh crore in October on festive demand boost
articles.summary: Gross Goods and Services Tax collections increased significantly in October 2026, driven by strong domestic activity and rising import revenues, according to government data released on November 1, 2026. Domestic sales revenues and import collections both registered substantial growth. After accounting for annual refunds, net collections also posted a notable double-digit increase for the month.
articles.description: Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore

articles.headline: Chief Justice of India calls for strengthening High Court public confidence
articles.title: CJI calls for strengthening public confidence in High Courts
articles.summary: Chief Justice of India Suyra Kant urged authorities to enhance public trust in High Courts during the platinum jubilee celebrations of the Kerala High Court on November 1, 2026. Speaking in Kochi, he emphasized that these institutions must remain accessible to vulnerable populations and transparent in case listings. The event was attended by Union Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal and Kerala High Court Chief Justice Soumen Sen.
articles.description: High Courts should continue to remain accessible to the vulnerable, attentive to the urgency of human suffering, and unwavering in its commitment to constitutional values, says Surya Kant

articles.headline: Israeli attacks on Gaza kill at least nine people
articles.title: Israeli attacks on Gaza kill at least nine people
articles.description: Israeli attacks on Gaza City and Khan Younis killed at least nine people on Sunday.

articles.headline: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar meets counterparts in Atlanta
articles.title: S. Jaishankar meets Russian, Polish, South Korean counterparts; discusses Ukraine, West Asia
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held bilateral discussions on October 31, 2026, with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, Polish Deputy Prime Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, and South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun. The meetings occurred on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta, focusing on the Ukraine conflict, West Asia, and multilateral ties before attending a college football game.
articles.description: The External Affairs Minister also met Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski

articles.headline: Israeli military attacks across Gaza kill at least eight Palestinians
articles.title: At least eight Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza
articles.summary: At least eight Palestinians were killed in Israeli military strikes across Gaza on Sunday, according to hospital sources. An attack in al-Mawasi targeted police officers, while a drone strike in Gaza City's Rimal neighbourhood killed three people, including a four-year-old child. Hamas condemned the strikes as a war crime, while the Israeli army stated it targeted a terrorist in southern Gaza.
articles.description: Four-year-old among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli drone attacks across the Gaza Strip.

articles.headline: US midterm elections record early voting surge with fifty million ballots
articles.title: More than 50 million votes cast in US midterm elections: What does it mean?
articles.summary: More than 50 million Americans cast early ballots ahead of the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, according to a University of Florida analysis. Early voting turnout surged significantly in states like Texas and South Carolina compared to 2022. The increase follows expanded mail-in and in-person voting options, higher democratic enthusiasm, and voter anxiety surrounding the cost-of-living crisis.
articles.description: A record number of early votes is cast as both parties campaign before Tuesday's polls.

articles.headline: Binance covers ninety percent of losses following massive cryptocurrency hack
articles.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance announced on October 31, 2026, that it covered ninety percent of the 6.3 billion dollars stolen in a recent cyberattack. Co-chief executive officer Richard Teng stated that corporate treasury funds were used to protect users, while analytics firms suspect North Korean hackers. Law enforcement and the company are continuing investigations and freezing assets.
articles.description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) says North Korea was responsible for the hack.

articles.headline: Iran and United States explore diplomatic opening amid military threats
articles.title: Iran and US explore diplomacy amid rising threats of war
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Qatari-mediated talks have created a potential diplomatic opening with the United States, reducing Tehran's Strait of Hormuz reopening offer to two days. However, both nations maintain military readiness as Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei demanded maximum deterrence against potential US and Israeli attacks on infrastructure following prior conflicts.
articles.description: Iran says could reopen Hormuz in shorter period if conditions met, as Trump says US still has targets to 'take care of'.

articles.headline: Cyclone Murasu approaches Andhra Pradesh coast with red alerts issued
articles.title: Cyclone ‘Murasu’ drums up fresh worry for Andhra after Arnab; red alert sounded in five districts
articles.summary: Cyclone Murasu is projected to strike the south coast between Nellore and Narsapur on the night of November 2, 2026, bringing winds up to 120 kmph. The India Meteorological Department issued red alerts for five districts as the state struggles to recover from Cyclone Arnab, which recently caused five deaths and widespread infrastructure damage.
articles.description: Cyclone Murasu is likely to cross the coast between Nellore and Narsapur on the night of November 2-3 as a severe cyclonic storm

articles.headline: Mamata Banerjee supports CJP and Gen Z at INDIA bloc rally
articles.title: At INDIA bloc rally, Mamata extends support to CJP, Gen Z; says Bengal victim of SIR
articles.summary: Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee addressed the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, 2026, expressing solidarity with CJP leadership and Gen Z activists. She accused the BJP of manipulating elections through the Special Intensive Revision exercise, criticised Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and called for united opposition against the ruling party.
articles.description: Taking a swipe at the SIR exercise, Mamata Banerjee described it as Special Intensive Relief to a party like the BJP

articles.headline: Champai Soren condemns alleged rape of woman inside Jharkhand police station
articles.title: Rape of woman inside police station, ‘repulsive image of jungle raj’ in Jharkhand: Champai Soren
articles.summary: Former Jharkhand Chief Minister Champai Soren criticised the alleged rape of a woman inside Gamharia police station in Seraikela-Kharswan district on November 1, 2026. The accused policeman, Niraj Lakra, was arrested, and five officers including station in-charge Sanjay Prasad were suspended for negligence after the victim was assaulted following a domestic dispute.
articles.description: The accused policeman, Niraj Lakra, has been arrested, and five policemen, including the officer-in-charge of Gamharia police station, Sanjay Prasad, were suspended on charges of dereliction of duty and negligence

articles.headline: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge attacks Prime Minister Narendra Modi at rally
articles.title: ‘Remove Modi to save democracy’: Congress chief Kharge attacks PM at INDIA bloc rally
articles.summary: Indian National Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged on November 1, 2026, that Bharatiya Janata Party governments at the Centre and in multiple states were formed on stolen mandates. Speaking at an opposition INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi, Kharge accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah of shielding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to disenfranchise marginalized citizens.
articles.description: Addressing INDIA bloc's rally at Ramlila Maidan on the "vote chori" charge, Mr. Kharge also accused Prime Minister Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah of shielding Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar

articles.headline: Cyclone Murasu forms over Bay of Bengal and threatens Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Cyclone ‘Murasu’ forms over Bay of Bengal, southern Odisha on high alert
articles.summary: Deep depression over the Bay of Bengal intensified into cyclonic storm Murasu on November 1, 2026. The India Meteorological Department forecasts landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast by November 3 with severe winds. Odisha disaster management officials ordered evacuations and issued high alerts across the southern region anticipating heavy rainfall from November 2 onward.
articles.description: The IMD said cyclone ‘Murasu’ is likely to make landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 3

articles.headline: German cost of living protests turn violent
articles.title: Shops looted as German cost-of-living protests turn violent
articles.summary: Demonstrations organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt over living costs, school underfunding, and military service turned violent in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne, and Hamburg. Police used water cannons as rioters looted shops, smashed windows, and targeted emergency workers with fireworks and stones. Hesse interior minister Roman Poseck condemned the infiltration of left-wing extremists into the protests.
articles.description: The protests in cities across Germany - including Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt - came on the same day hundreds of thousands also protested in France.

articles.headline: Thousands demonstrate in New Delhi demanding election chief resign
articles.title: Thousands rally in New Delhi to demand India’s election chief resign
articles.summary: Thousands of protesters marched in New Delhi on November 1, 2026, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over controversial electoral roll revisions. Led by Indian National Congress politician Rahul Gandhi, the demonstration at Ramlila Maidan followed weeks of unrest sparked by the removal of over 130 million names from voter lists, which critics argue disproportionately targets minorities.
articles.description: Hundreds of police, some carrying batons and shields, are deployed around the rally site.

articles.headline: Iranian officials discuss diplomatic proposals with Qatari mediators
articles.title: Mediators continue US-Iran negotiations amid war rhetoric: What we know
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi announced that officials are discussing a two-day plan with Qatari mediators in Doha to reopen the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing military tensions with the United States. While expressing openness to dialogue if Washington lifts recent sanctions and reduces regional military presence, Iranian leaders warned that armed forces remain fully prepared for renewed conflict.
articles.description: Trump says latest talks 'going fine'; Iranian leaders say they favour diplomacy but are ready to respond to US attacks.

articles.headline: India cuts petrol export duty to nil and raises diesel levy
articles.title: Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre
articles.summary: The Indian government reduced export duty on petrol to nil on October 31, 2026, while increasing levies on diesel and aviation turbine fuel by three rupees and fifty paise per litre respectively. The fortnightly adjustment aims to ensure domestic fuel availability amidst global supply constraints. Data from analytics provider Kpler indicated that national diesel exports reached seven hundred thousand barrels per day in October.
articles.description: The government’s fortnightly review raised the export levy on diesel to ₹11.5 per litre from ₹8.5 and on aviation turbine fuel to ₹11 per litre from ₹10.5, while India’s diesel exports touched 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025, according to Kpler

articles.headline: Qatari liquefied natural gas carrier struck by unidentified objects in Gulf
articles.title: Qatar LNG carrier struck by ‘unidentified objects’ in Gulf
articles.summary: Unidentified objects struck the Al Mayeda liquefied natural gas carrier in the Gulf, according to the Qatar Gas Transport Company. The vessel suffered no crew injuries or environmental damage and remains operational. This incident follows more than one hundred commercial ship attacks since the United States and Israel conflict with Iran began in February.
articles.description: Qatar Gas Transport Company says no injuries or environmental damage.

articles.headline: Pakistan warns Afghanistan that cross-border terrorism remains a red line.
articles.title: Terrorism is 'red line': Pakistan tells Afghanistan as it warns of action against cross-border threats
articles.summary: Pakistan stated on October 31, 2026, that it reserves the right to take necessary measures against cross-border security threats originating from Afghanistan. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting accused the Afghan Taliban administration of inaction regarding militancy. The statement followed remarks from Afghan spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, who argued that Islamabad lacked readiness for dialogue and shifted blame rather than resolving bilateral tensions.
articles.description: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting of Pakistan, on Saturday, accused the Afghan Taliban leadership of refusing to address militancy emanating from Afghan soil and instead shifting blame on Islamabad for the deterioration in bilateral ties

articles.headline: US voters head to polls amid tight congressional races and economic concerns
articles.title: US midterms: 2 days to go – Who leads in the polls as Trump rallies
articles.summary: Democratic and Republican leaders made final campaign pushes ahead of United States midterm elections featuring crucial Senate races. Polling indicates Democrats lead nationally while addressing voter anxieties regarding cost of living and the ongoing conflict involving Iran. Meanwhile, over fifty one million Americans have already cast ballots through mail-in systems or early voting locations.
articles.description: Democrats remain ahead in national polls as Trump and candidates make their final push in the days before polling day.

articles.headline: Trump at Halloween party ‘as himself’ says he’s ‘in no hurry’ with Iran
articles.title: Trump at Halloween party ‘as himself’ says he’s ‘in no hurry’ with Iran
articles.description: Trump, who came to his Halloween party dressed as himself, says US not in a hurry to make a decision on striking Iran.

articles.headline: Iran security chief says US letter signals ‘positive’ shift
articles.title: Iran security chief says US letter signals ‘positive’ shift
articles.description: US Vice-President JD Vance has sent a letter to Iran’s security chief in a reported effort to revive talks.

articles.headline: President Trump says United States still has one or two targets in Iran
articles.title: President Trump says U.S. still has ‘one or two targets’ in Iran
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated on October 31, 2026, that much of Iran's military has been incapacitated, though one or two sites remain. Meanwhile, Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned of severe reprisals against American and Israeli assets. Mediators from Qatar are currently engaged in diplomatic efforts in Tehran to prevent further escalation of the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: The President said the United States is not in a hurry to take offensive action because it had already decimated Iran’s military and nuclear programme

articles.headline: Mass displacement and extensive destruction continue across Gaza, the West Bank and Lebanon.
articles.title: Israel’s war on homes: From Hebron to Gaza and southern Lebanon
articles.summary: Military operations and widespread demolitions have displaced thousands of residents and destroyed infrastructure across the occupied West Bank, Gaza, and southern Lebanon. According to United Nations agencies and international organizations, hundreds of thousands of people remain displaced amid ongoing conflict. Human rights officials warn that the widespread devastation and forced expulsions raise serious concerns regarding violations of international law.
articles.description: From Hebron to Gaza to southern Lebanon, Israel is tearing down homes, and, with them, families' hopes of return.

articles.headline: Gaza healthcare workers face severe trauma and bereavement during the war.
articles.title: Gaza doctors struggle with bereavement, overwork, trauma amid genocidal war
articles.summary: Medical personnel in Gaza experience profound psychological distress while working under extreme pressure during the ongoing conflict. According to official reports, numerous healthcare workers have been killed, detained, or suffered personal bereavement and displacement. Medical professionals struggle to balance humanitarian duties with untreated trauma amid severe staff shortages and a lack of adequate psychological support systems.
articles.description: Doctors and nurses struggle to cope with the horrors they endured during the height of the Gaza war.

articles.headline: Indian opposition coalition plans massive Delhi rally demanding election chief resignation
articles.title: India's opposition holds mega rally seeking election chief's resignation
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of people are expected to gather at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi for a mega opposition rally demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Organised by the Congress party and supported by the Cockroach Janta Party, the protest follows a voter-list revision exercise that removed 130 million names from draft rolls across India.
articles.description: Thousands gathered in the heart of delhi, calling for the chief election commissioner to step down.

articles.headline: US judge dismisses Donald Trump defamation lawsuit against Wall Street Journal
articles.title: ‘Epstein Files’: U.S. Judge dismisses Trump lawsuit against Wall Street Journal
articles.summary: A United States judge dismissed President Donald Trump's ten billion dollar defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal on October thirty first. The court ruled that Mr Trump failed to establish actual malice regarding a published twenty twenty five report about his alleged two thousand three letter to Jeffrey Epstein. Meanwhile, the administration faced separate legal challenges over a proposed capital arch.
articles.description: Donald Trump had sued for $10 billion after the newspaper’s story was published in July 2025 detailing the President’s alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman

articles.headline: Infant deaths in Attappady renew concerns over tribal health and socioeconomic conditions
articles.title: How infant deaths in Keralam’s Attappady expose a deep-rooted health, social crisis
articles.summary: The recent deaths of 12 infants in Attappady have highlighted a persistent child health crisis affecting tribal communities in Keralam. Figures from tribal activists indicate that 124 infants have died in the region since 2011 alongside numerous abortions and stillbirths. While the State government has initiated an expert assessment, tribal organizations stress that solutions require addressing broader nutritional, maternal health, landlessness, and socioeconomic challenges.
articles.description: 12 infants, including 10 tribals, have died in Attappady this year, sparking a political row as the State government orders an expert probe. Tribal activists say the crisis demands action beyond healthcare, addressing malnutrition, anaemia and deep-rooted social issues

articles.headline: Social media users in India report blocked posts amid protests
articles.title: ‘Unavailable in India’: Why are social media posts being blocked amid protests? | Explained
articles.summary: Social media users in India have reported widespread blocking of posts, reels, and accounts across platforms such as Instagram, Facebook, and X. According to reports, automated restrictions were implemented under the Information Technology Rules of 2021. This development comes amid nationwide protests against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
articles.description: MeitY’s advisory to Meta, shorter takedown deadlines under amended IT Rules, and platforms’ own enforcement policies have brought renewed scrutiny of how online content is blocked, and what recourse users have

articles.headline: Opposition alliance conducts symbolic public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
articles.title: INDIA bloc holds symbolic ‘public impeachment’ of CEC Gyanesh Kumar on six charges
articles.summary: Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance leaders unanimously adopted a motion during a parliamentary simulation at Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence. Opposition figures accused the election official of manipulating rolls and conspiring with ruling leaders. Senior politicians warned that administrative staff implementing alleged electoral irregularities would face future accountability.
articles.description: Move reflects the closure of institutional avenues, says LoP Rahul Gandhi; terms it a political weapon against all who colluded to destroy votes; warns ECI officials that they are first target; says CEC should be tried for treason

articles.headline: INDIA bloc supporters gather at Ramlila Maidan for Chalo Dilli protest
articles.title: INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli’ protest: Supporters gather at Ramlila Maidan, across capital
articles.summary: Opposition alliance supporters began gathering at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan for the Chalo Dilli protest on November first to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The demonstration follows allegations of widespread voter roll manipulation. Authorities deployed over four thousand police personnel across the capital while organisers prepared barricades and stages for the anticipated crowds.
articles.description: Many supporters arrived in Delhi, while several others had reached the national capital on October 31, 2026 or earlier as parties mobilised their cadres from different states for the protest

articles.headline: Manisha Bhanwala wins India’s first women’s wrestling world title in Astana
articles.title: Manisha Bhanwala: The 29-year-old who ended India’s wait for a women’s wrestling world title
articles.summary: Wrestler Manisha Bhanwala secured a historic gold medal in the 59kg freestyle category at the World Wrestling Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan, defeating American competitor Abigail Nette on October 31, 2026. This victory marks India's first-ever women's world title in the sport. The 29-year-old athlete from Jind, Haryana, dedicated her triumph to her late father Suresh Bhanwala, capping an unprecedented campaign that also featured silver medals from teammates Neelam Sirohi and Kajal Dhochak.
articles.description: From a village in Haryana to the pinnacle of international wrestling, Manisha Bhanwala scripted history in Kazakhstan, becoming India’s first woman world champion

articles.headline: Arab citizens surge to polls in high-turnout Israeli election
articles.title: Ra’am and Joint List | The surge of the other
articles.summary: Israel recorded a high voter turnout of seventy-seven percent during its recent general election, driven by an overwhelming mobilization among Arab citizens. The Joint List and the United Arab List secured a combined nineteen seats in parliament. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu criticized the surge, while Arab leaders sought representation against policies they argue perpetuate discrimination.
articles.description: Israel’s Arab parties made historic gains in elections but uncertainty remains whether the opposition bloc would join hands with them to form a government

articles.headline: World Bank reports rapid poverty reduction in India over the past decade
articles.title: India made ‘remarkable progress’ in reducing poverty: World Bank
articles.summary: According to an October 2026 report by the World Bank, India achieved rapid poverty reduction between 2011 and 2023, lifting approximately 496 million people out of poverty as extreme poverty rates declined. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman attributed these improvements to strong consumption growth, rising employment among women, and expanded social welfare programs. However, the report also highlighted ongoing challenges, including wage disparities and a rise in youth unemployment.
articles.description: Report says the country saw one of the fastest reductions in poverty in the world; extreme poverty fell to 2.6% in 2023 from 27.1% in 2011, driven by government transfers and rising employment

articles.headline: Foreign secretary Vikram Misri attributes Chinese harshness to pandemic stigma
articles.title: Global criticism during COVID-19 hardened China’s attitude towards world: Foreign Secretary Misri
articles.summary: India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri stated on October 31, 2026, that global criticism and a sense of stigmatization during the COVID-19 pandemic caused China to adopt a harsh attitude toward the international community and enforce strict internal lockdowns. Speaking at the Iqwat Global Business Conclave, Misri reflected on his tenure as ambassador to China, recalling the immense challenges posed by bilateral stress, travel restrictions, and the 2020 Galwan Valley confrontation.
articles.description: Misri also recalled that he faced a major challenge during his posting in China as Ambassador, when India and China had an unprecedented confrontation in eastern Ladakh's Galwan Valley

articles.headline: What we know about latest efforts to end US war on Iran
articles.title: What we know about latest efforts to end US war on Iran
articles.description: The foreign ministers of the US and Iran say a diplomatic end to the war is still possible.

articles.headline: Serbian railway station canopy collapse ends ruling party rule
articles.title: Student List | The young Serb unrest
articles.summary: The collapse of a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad Railway station in Serbia killed sixteen people, including two young children. Widespread public outrage over allegations of corruption and government negligence in the recently reconstructed state-funded project ultimately brought an end to fourteen years of rule by the Serbian Progressive Party led by Aleksandar Vucic.
articles.description: Serbia’s student protesters, who built a blockade movement against corruption and political establishment, brought down the government of Aleksandar Vučić

articles.headline: Lula da Silva wins historic Brazilian presidential runoff election
articles.title: Lula da Silva | The Pele of Brazil’s politics
articles.summary: Lula da Silva made history by becoming the first Brazilian president to finish second in the initial election round and subsequently win the presidential runoff. During the campaign, opponent Flavio Bolsonaro weaponized an old injury involving da Silva losing a finger while working in a factory, prompting a sharp response from the Workers Party leader.
articles.description: The left-wing leader’s victory in Brazil, after finishing second in the first round, reflects the deep roots of the Workers’ Party, which built its support base through resistance to the military dictatorship in the early 1980s, as well as the declining appeal of Bolsonarismo

articles.headline: U.S. President Donald Trump delays decision on fresh Iran strikes
articles.title: Rubio says U.S. yet to decide on new Iran strikes
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump has not yet decided on launching new military strikes against Iran amid stalled peace talks, according to Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Speaking on Saturday in Atlanta, Georgia, Rubio stated that the administration remains open to a diplomatic solution despite ongoing tensions and Iranian targeting of commercial vessels.
articles.description: Iran’s supreme leader October 31, 2026 warned the United States and Israel against launching new attacks, following threats to resume strikes after crucial elections

articles.headline: India announces nationwide population census schedule for early 2027
articles.title: Population census to be conducted from January 25 to February 28 except in snow-bound and poll-bound States
articles.summary: The Indian government has announced that the nationwide population census will take place from January 25, 2027, to February 28, 2027. According to a Gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs on October 30, 2026, the exercise will exclude specific snow-bound and poll-bound regions, while setting the official reference date as March 1, 2027, to determine demographic statistics accurately.
articles.description: Reference date for population census will be 00:00 hours of March 1, 2027; census will not be held in Manipur, Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Uttarakhand, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and J&K

articles.headline: FBI links North Korea to record crypto heist
articles.title: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3bn crypto heist from Binance
articles.summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation has attributed the theft of six point three billion dollars in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance to North Korea. Authorities stated the hackers laundered funds by converting them into Ethereum. Meanwhile, Binance replaced ninety percent of the stolen amount using internal funds and its Secure Asset Fund for Users reserve to protect customers.
articles.description: Crypto firm Binance says it has covered 90 percent of losses from the multibillion-dollar hack.

articles.headline: UN rights office warns of ongoing displacement and ethnic cleansing in Gaza
articles.title: Ethnic cleansing fears rise as Israel squeezes space in Gaza: UN
articles.summary: The United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights warned on Friday that Israeli military operations continue to displace Palestinians into a shrinking portion of the Gaza Strip, raising serious concerns of ethnic cleansing. The agency reported extensive destruction of civilian infrastructure and recent attacks on displacement camps, noting that ongoing conflict has caused significant casualties since October 2023.
articles.description: Israeli forces are treating the 'Yellow Line', which is encroaching westward, as 'a kill zone', the OHCHR says.

articles.headline: Thousands in Israel urge Eisenkot-Arab deal
articles.title: Thousands rally in Israel urging ‘Jewish-Arab’ coalition to oust Netanyahu
articles.summary: Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Tel Aviv to pressure opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot into forming a coalition with Arab parties to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Following an election deadlock where Netanyahu and Eisenkot fell short of a majority, Arab-led parties secured nineteen seats, creating a potential path to a sixty-seven seat majority government.
articles.description: In a counterprotest, Netanyahu supporters demand that Israel should not have a government with 'terrorists'.

articles.headline: Three killed in Manipur gunfight
articles.title: 3 killed in gunfight between rival groups in Manipur's Noney
articles.summary: Three individuals belonging to the Kuki community died during a multi-hour gunfight between rival armed groups in Manipur's Noney district. The clash erupted at Kekru Naga village, prompting police to implement security measures. The Kuki Inpi Manipur apex body strongly condemned the killings and alleged that Naga militant groups were responsible for the violent incident.
articles.description: Meanwhile, the Kuki Inpi Manipur (KIM), the apex body of the Kuki community, strongly condemned the killing of the three youths

articles.headline: Neocloud firms spark AI bubble fears
articles.title: These firms you've never heard of are feeding fears the AI bubble could burst
articles.summary: Neocloud data centre companies like CoreWeave and Nebius are facing investor scrutiny over heavy debt loads and financial stability as artificial intelligence spending forecasts fluctuate. Industry analysts warn that many independent operators could face acquisition or closure amid rising interest rates and heavy hardware costs, though demand for computing power from major artificial intelligence developers remains high.
articles.description: The amount of debt held by data centres is measured in the tens of billions of pounds.

articles.headline: Student movements and youth turnout unseat leaders in Serbia and Hungary
articles.title: How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
articles.summary: Popular movements led by tech-savvy youth ousted long-serving leaders Viktor Orbán in Hungary and Aleksandar Vučić in Serbia after record turnouts of 79 percent and 69 percent respectively. Digital monitoring tools and cross-border cooperation helped detect electoral fraud. Both former leaders now face potential corruption prosecution following parallel political downfalls driven by public discontent.
articles.description: Defeat for Serbia's Aleksandar Vučiċ in last weekend's vote was a carbon copy of Viktor Orbán's fall in Hungary.

articles.headline: UN commission accuses Israel of ongoing war crimes and genocide in Gaza and West Bank
articles.title: Israeli forces committed war crimes, genocide even after Gaza ceasefire: UN Commission
articles.summary: The Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory reported that Israeli authorities continue committing severe human rights violations, including war crimes and genocide, despite the October 2025 ceasefire. Chaired by Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, the United Nations body stated that over 75,000 Palestinians have died since October 7, 2023, while Israeli Permanent Representative Danny Danon strongly rejected the allegations as historical fiction.
articles.description: In Gaza, Israeli forces have continued expanding their territorial control, resulting in the killing and injuring of Palestinian civilians, including children, who approach or cross the Yellow Line, which separates Israel- military controlled Gaza from the Palestine-ruled parts of the enclave, Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar said.

articles.headline: Federal judge blocks Trump administration from threatening election officials
articles.title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials
articles.summary: United States District Judge Trina Thompson ordered the federal government to halt threats of criminal charges against local and state election officials processing ballots. The Department of Justice previously demanded officials set aside thousands of voter ballots allegedly cast by non-citizens. Civil rights groups filed a legal complaint challenging the administration actions ahead of elections.
articles.description: The order comes after election officials received letters demanding they set aside the ballots of possible non-citizen voters.

articles.headline: Gen Z-led protests in Germany turn violent
articles.title: Gen Z-led protests in Germany turn violent
articles.description: Protesters clashed with police as thousands took to the streets across 34 cities in Germany.

articles.headline: Judge dismisses Donald Trump defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal
articles.title: Trump loses legal battle over Epstein-linked Wall Street Journal case
articles.summary: United States District Judge Darrin Gayles permanently dismissed Donald Trump's ten billion dollar defamation lawsuit against Rupert Murdoch and The Wall Street Journal. The judge concluded that the president failed to establish actual malice regarding an article that linked him to Jeffrey Epstein. Filed in Miami on July 18, 2025, the complaint contested coverage of a 2003 birthday note.
articles.description: Judge permanently drops Trump's $10bn WSJ lawsuit, ruling he failed to prove actual malice in the newspaper's reporting.

articles.headline: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
articles.title: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
articles.description: More than 320,000 people demonstrated across France against the rising cost of living and poor public services, with clashes between some protesters and police.

articles.headline: Erdogan and Zelenskyy push for Black Sea shipping security
articles.title: Turkiye’s Erdogan urges Russia and Ukraine to stop Black Sea attacks
articles.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urged Russia and Ukraine to halt attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea during a joint news conference in Istanbul. Erdogan and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy agreed to collaborate on establishing a new grain corridor through the waterway to restore safe navigation, address global food security threats, and revive diplomatic peace efforts.
articles.description: Turkish president hosts Zelenskyy in Istanbul as the two leaders agree to work on a new Black Sea grain corridor.

articles.headline: Trump announces immediate Russian diesel supplies following talks with Putin
articles.title: Trump says Russia to immediately supply diesel to U.S. after talks with Putin
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated on October 9, 2026, that Russia will supply hundreds of thousands of tonnes of diesel fuel to the American market following a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The move aims to lower domestic fuel prices amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran. However, the agreement faced severe condemnation from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and various American lawmakers who argued the policy supports Moscow's economy.
articles.description: The surprise announcement comes against the backdrop of a U.S. law seeking to impose steep tariffs against top purchasers of Russian oil and gas

articles.headline: Ukrainian evacuees arrive in Chernihiv after fleeing Oleshky
articles.title: 'We came back from hell', say Ukrainians after years in Russia-occupied front-line city
articles.summary: Hundreds of residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied front-line city of Oleshky arrived at a military facility in Chernihiv following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. Survivors described enduring years of severe shelling, severe food shortages, and dangerous minefields before crossing through southern Russia and Belarus to escape the devastated region.
articles.description: One evacuated couple says they crossed minefields in Oleshky in search of food.

articles.headline: Palestinians ‘Stealing their own olives’
articles.title: Palestinians ‘Stealing their own olives’
articles.description: In the occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers have turned olive harvesting into a deadly activity for Palestinians.

articles.headline: French police deploy tear gas as hundreds of thousands protest
articles.title: Tension and clashes as hundreds of thousands protest again in France
articles.summary: Security forces clashed with demonstrators in Paris and Lyon during the third consecutive weekend of nationwide rallies concerning the cost of living and school conditions. Organisers estimated nearly half a million participants, while the French Ministry of Interior reported 320,000 attendees and at least 290 arrests. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu held meetings with student unions as similar youth-led protests also emerged in Germany, Spain, and Italy.
articles.description: Authorities say 320,000 march on third consecutive weekend of demonstrations over cost of living and state of schools.

articles.headline: Russian security service says United States warned about potential Moscow attack
articles.title: Russia’s FSB says U.S. warned Russia of possible Moscow attack
articles.summary: Russia’s Federal Security Service stated that American partner channels provided details regarding preparations for a terrorist strike in the capital. The U.S. Embassy in Moscow separately noted a credible threat at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve, leading authorities to temporarily close the palace park. Officials recalled a similar 2024 warning preceding the Crocus City Hall mass shooting.
articles.description: The ‌U.S. Embassy had warned that extremists ​had imminent plans for an attack in Moscow

articles.headline: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky arrive in Belarus on route to Ukraine
articles.title: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city
articles.summary: Civilians evacuated from the devastated city of Oleshky landed in Gomel, Belarus, following a local ceasefire brokered by United States First Lady Melania Trump. The residents endured severe conditions without food, water, or electricity, with some surviving on garden weeds. The humanitarian truce allowed mine-clearing operations along escape routes before buses transported citizens toward Ukrainian territory.
articles.description: Oleshky residents had been without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.

articles.headline: Israeli attacks kill four Palestinians in Gaza despite ongoing ceasefire
articles.title: At least four Palestinians killed in Gaza as Israeli attacks continue
articles.summary: Ongoing military operations across the enclave resulted in multiple fatalities, including a teacher in Nuseirat and two girls in Khan Younis. Gaza health officials reported that recent casualties raised the death toll under the current ceasefire to 1,580. Meanwhile, United Nations human rights monitors warned that forced displacements and infrastructure destruction continued to spark ethnic cleansing concerns.
articles.description: Israel carried out several attacks in Gaza, including shelling the Nuseirat refugee camp.

articles.headline: Weather department warns Andhra Pradesh may face another severe cyclonic storm
articles.title: After ‘Arnab’, Andhra Pradesh may face another severe cyclonic storm
articles.summary: Meteorologists predicted that a developing weather system over the Andaman Sea will intensify into a severe storm by November 2. The India Meteorological Department stated the system could make landfall in Andhra Pradesh with winds reaching 120 kmph. Disaster management authorities advised fishermen to stay ashore as heavy rainfall threatened districts statewide.
articles.description: The depression over Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 2; landfall is expected between Narsapur and Nellore on November 3, with maximum wind speed of 120 kmph

articles.headline: Ashutosh Dixit assumes charge as Indian Chief of Air Staff
articles.title: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit takes charge as 29th Chief of Air Staff
articles.summary: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit assumed command as the new Chief of Air Staff, succeeding Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh following his retirement. Dixit brings four decades of service and over 3,500 flying hours across 20 aircraft types to the role, having previously served as Vice Chief of the force and Chief of Integrated Defence Staff.
articles.description: The IAF accorded a ceremonial guard of honour to the outgoing Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh at the Race Course Air Force Station before he handed over the baton to Ashutosh Dixit

articles.headline: Quad foreign ministers meet in Atlanta to review regional progress
articles.title: Quad delivering results for people in Indo-Pacific: Rubio
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio met External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, Japan's Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi, and Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong in Atlanta on October 31, 2026. According to Mr. Rubio, the officials reviewed Indo-Pacific cooperation and supply chains ahead of an upcoming summit in the Philippines. Mr. Jaishankar noted that the talks also focused on strengthening bilateral relations.
articles.description: The group reviewed progress in turning shared priorities into real benefits for the Indo-Pacific region

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh chief minister orders high alert over cyclone threat
articles.title: Naidu calls for high alert as another cyclone threat looms over Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to accelerate restoration works following Cyclone Arnab and prepare for a potential new cyclone on October 31, 2026. A depression in the Bay of Bengal threatens south coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema with heavy rainfall from November 2 to November 4. Authorities were instructed to monitor satellite data and provide compensation for agricultural losses.
articles.description: Depression over southeast Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into a cyclone by November 1; officials told to monitor its movement every six hours and expedite restoration works in cyclone-hit areas

articles.headline: Union government releases tax devolution instalment of 1.09 lakh crore rupees
articles.title: Centre releases additional instalment of tax devolution of ₹1.09 lakh crore to states
articles.summary: The Union government released an additional tax devolution instalment exceeding 1.09 lakh crore rupees to state governments on October 31, 2026. The Finance Ministry stated that the funds aim to support state development expenditure and accelerate capital spending ahead of the festive season. States regularly receive forty-one percent of centrally collected taxes across fourteen annual instalments.
articles.description: This is in addition to the regular monthly devolution and the second additional instalment this financial year

articles.headline: Quad ministers express grave concern over economic coercion and overproduction
articles.title: Quad ministers express ‘grave concerns’ over economic coercion
articles.summary: Foreign ministers from the United States, India, Japan, and Australia issued joint concerns regarding economic coercion and non-market policies during a meeting in Atlanta on October 31, 2026. Without naming countries, the alliance warned that arbitrary export restrictions and overcapacity disrupt global supply chains. The officials also emphasized the importance of preserving navigational rights and maritime security in critical global sea lanes.
articles.description: "The four ministers expressed grave concerns regarding economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions," said a statement from the Quad alliance in Atlanta, Georgia.

articles.headline: U.S. approves Patriot missiles sale to Ukraine as delivery timelines remain uncertain
articles.title: Trump admin approves potential Patriot missiles sale to Ukraine
articles.summary: The United States State Department green-lit the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine following weeks of complaints regarding dwindling interceptor supplies. While the approval goes to Congress for review, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that deliveries could take years. The weapons sale will be funded by donations from allies rather than United States funds.
articles.description: The approval, which goes to Congress for review, comes after weeks of complaints by Ukrainian authorities that its supplies of the interceptor missiles were dwindling

articles.headline: Beyond Cyclone Arnab: can India tackle the growing cost of natural disasters? | Insight India
articles.title: Beyond Cyclone Arnab: can India tackle the growing cost of natural disasters? | Insight India
articles.description: Cyclone Arnab hit the coast of Andhra Pradesh this week. In preparation, authorities evacuated people, halted transportation services and alerted disaster response forces. This is just the first cyclone of the northeast monsoon season. As climate change threatens to bring increasingly intense cyclones and other natural disasters, will India’s current disaster management programme be able to handle the social and economic costs I?n this episode, Sonikka Loganathan speaks to Safi Ahsan Rizvi, former Adviser to the National Disaster Management Authority, about what goes into disaster management, the costs to the economy and vulnerable populations, and how India has improved its strategy since 1999.

articles.headline: Wrestler Manisha Bhanwala secures historic World championship gold medal in Astana
articles.title: A dream come true moment for Manisha
articles.summary: Manisha Bhanwala became the first Indian woman wrestler to win a World championship gold by defeating the United States competitor Abigail Elizabeth Nette 8-6 in the final on October 31, 2026. Competing in the 59kg category in Astana, the 29-year-old athlete rebounded from a disappointing Asian Games performance. She dedicated the victory to her late father, helping propel the Indian women's team to a fifth-place finish.
articles.description: She becomes the first-ever Indian woman wrestler to land a World championship gold in Astana

articles.headline: Democratic Republic of Congo records over 5,000 deaths in deadliest Ebola outbreak
articles.title: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak
articles.summary: Government data shows that more than 5,000 people have died from an ongoing Ebola outbreak across eight provinces in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Public health officials reported over 10,300 confirmed cases with a fatality rate of 48.6%. The World Health Organization stated that greater access to affected areas and key control measures are needed to end the epidemic.
articles.description: Government data shows that more than 10,000 people have contracted the rare virus.

articles.headline: Central teams inspect cyclone Arnab damage in Andhra Pradesh as relief sought
articles.title: Central teams assess cyclone Arnab damage in East Godavari, Konaseema as Naidu seeks ₹4,600 crore in relief
articles.summary: Two Inter-Ministerial Central teams inspected cyclone Arnab-hit regions across East Godavari, West Godavari, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema districts on October 31, 2026, evaluating agricultural and infrastructural losses. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu previously estimated total damages at ₹4,600 crore following the October 29 landfall. The assessment aims to verify extensive destruction to paddy fields, horticulture crops, and thousands of houses and fishing boats.
articles.description: Two Inter-Ministerial Central teams inspect damage to crops, houses, public infrastructure and fishing assets in the two districts; West Godavari reports extensive paddy, aquaculture and fishing boat losses

articles.headline: Iran foreign minister calls United States outreach positive while outlining conditions
articles.title: Iran FM says US outreach a ‘positive step’ as delegation in Qatar for talks
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described a diplomatic overture from United States Vice President JD Vance as a positive step during a statement on October 31, 2026. While an Iranian delegation visited Doha for consultations mediated by Qatar, Araghchi stated that direct meetings with American officials are unnecessary at this stage. Tehran demands the lifting of specific sanctions, reduced regional forces, and the release of frozen funds before implementing proposals.
articles.description: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi tells Al Jazeera Tehran doesn't rule out attack, is ‘prepared for all scenarios’.

articles.headline: South Africa defeats Australia by 176 runs to claim Test series victory
articles.title: Harmer shines as South Africa wins third Test against Australia to claim series 2-1
articles.summary: Simon Harmer claimed career-best figures of 6-16 as South Africa dismissed Australia for 111 runs on October 31, 2026, securing a 176-run victory in the third Test in Cape Town. The win clinched the series 2-1 for the Proteas, who rose to the top of the International Cricket Council rankings. Harmer finished the match with ten wickets, while bowler Kagiso Rabada achieved his 350th Test wicket during the final day.
articles.description: The Proteas rallied from 1-0 down in the first Test series between the teams in South Africa since the ‘Sandpapergate’ scandal in 2018.

articles.headline: Iran supreme leader warns United States and Israel against new attacks
articles.title: Iran’s Supreme Leader warns U.S., Israel against new attacks
articles.summary: Mojtaba Khamenei warned the United States and Israel during a meeting with senior military commanders on October 31, 2026. The supreme leader instructed forces to ensure any threat receives an immediate and geographically unrestricted response. The remarks coincided with diplomatic talks in Tehran involving Qatari officials addressing a letter from United States Vice President JD Vance.
articles.description: According to the statement, Mr. Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that "any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response".

articles.headline: Israel's parliamentary elections end in deadlock as neither major bloc secures majority
articles.title: Israel voted for Israel: Why Gaza wasn’t on the ballot
articles.summary: Israel remains politically deadlocked after the October 27 polls failed to deliver a 61-seat majority for any coalition, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp securing 53 seats. Despite massive voter turnout, the ongoing conflict in Gaza and related humanitarian crises were largely absent from campaign debates, which focused instead on domestic issues like judicial reforms and military exemptions. Analysts noted that military occupation and security fundamentally shaped voter perspectives across the political spectrum.
articles.description: Despite genocide, regional war and isolation, Israel's election revealed little appetite for political alternatives.

articles.headline: Andy Burnham considers formal slavery apology while ruling out reparations
articles.title: Burnham opens door to formal apology for Britain’s slave trade
articles.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated he is open to issuing a formal state apology regarding Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade, ahead of a Commonwealth leaders summit in Antigua and Barbuda. Speaking on Friday, Burnham rejected financial reparations but proposed an international initiative to reduce debt burdens for poorer nations, supported by former Prime Minister Gordon Brown. Caribbean leaders welcomed talks on broader cooperation.
articles.description: UK Prime Minister rules out financial reparations, despite longstanding Caribbean demands.

articles.headline: Yemen conflict displacement reaches 290,000 as fighting intensifies
articles.title: New Yemen fighting displaces 290,000, says UN, with pregnant women at risk
articles.summary: At least 290,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since August due to escalating conflict between government forces and Houthi rebels, according to the United Nations humanitarian office. The violence has heavily impacted Taiz governorate and caused severe shortages, while pregnant women and refugees face acute risks. Meanwhile, military operations and reported missile attacks continue across multiple fronts, including near Saudi Arabia and the presidential palace in Aden.
articles.description: A new outbreak in fighting in Yemen has forced tens of thousands of people from their homes.

articles.headline: Alphabet revenue growth highlights heavy artificial intelligence infrastructure spending costs
articles.title: Why investors are worried despite Alphabet’s 25% revenue growth and Google Cloud’s revenue more than doubling | Explained
articles.summary: The partial text notes that Alphabet reported strong growth in the September quarter while highlighting significant financial costs dedicated to keeping pace with the artificial intelligence sector. Heavy investments in computing infrastructure are required to develop artificial intelligence models. Additionally, artificial intelligence tools are changing user interaction with Google Search, creating questions regarding future advertising revenue generation and capital expenditure returns.
articles.description: Google’s parent company is investing heavily in artificial intelligence infrastructure as its cloud business expands. But the spending is weighing on cash flow, while AI-powered search raises questions about the future of its advertising business

articles.headline: Iranian lawmakers call for nuclear treaty withdrawal amid ongoing conflict
articles.title: Iran lawmakers call for withdrawal from NPT: Will we have war or peace?
articles.summary: Several Iranian legislators have urged the country to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and alter its nuclear doctrine following heavy costs from war and sanctions. The demands arrive as the conflict enters its ninth month and Qatari mediators pursue peace talks involving the United States. While Iranian leaders have not formally responded, the International Atomic Energy Agency previously raised concerns regarding Tehran's nuclear compliance.
articles.description: Withdrawal from the nuclear treaty doses not mean that Iran would build a nuclear weapon, observers say.

articles.headline: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
articles.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
articles.summary: The United States State Department approved a 2.1 billion dollar sale of 500 Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine to defend against Russian aerial attacks. European allies and Canada funded the purchase entirely, with Lockheed Martin serving as the principal contractor. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that the country was facing critical shortages as Russian ballistic missile strikes intensified across multiple regions.
articles.description: The American-made interceptors are the only effective weapon for downing Russia's ballistic missiles.

articles.headline: Iran warns of unfettered retaliation amid ongoing diplomatic efforts
articles.title: Iran warns of unfettered retaliation if attacked as mediators try for peace
articles.summary: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered armed forces to prepare for an immediate, geographically unrestricted response if attacked again. Mediators from Qatar held talks in Tehran on Friday to prevent a new war as tensions persist over maritime security and regional conflicts. Meanwhile, local authorities reported that US drone strikes bombed fishing boats south of Qeshm island, injuring several fishermen.
articles.description: Iran’s supreme leader says Tehran’s potential response will not be restricted by geography.

articles.headline: Hundreds of evacuees from Oleshky arrive in Belarus
articles.title: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky arrive in Ukraine via Belarus
articles.summary: Evacuees from the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky have arrived in Gomel, Belarus, via four planes as part of an evacuation mission supported by United States First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo XIV. The civilians crossed the border during a regional truce that allows residents to choose between Ukrainian-held territory, Russian-held territory, or remaining in the city with replenished medical supplies.
articles.description: Four planes transporting evacuees from the war-ravaged city arrived in Belarus's Gomel earlier on Saturday.

articles.headline: Jio Platforms raises 3.2 billion dollars in stock market debut
articles.title: How Ambani’s Jio became India’s second-largest company
articles.summary: Jio Platforms achieved India's largest initial public offering by raising 3.2 billion dollars, causing its shares to surge 21 percent on Wednesday and valuing the company at 131.5 billion dollars. Backed by Meta and Google, the company serves over 530 million customers, though its rapid rise since 2016 has heavily concentrated India's telecommunications market and sparked intense industry competition.
articles.description: Jio makes India’s largest-ever stock market debut, raising $3.2bn in IPO.

articles.headline: Democrats target four Senate seats to overcome Republican majority
articles.title: Can Democrats win the US Senate? 10 key midterm races to watch
articles.summary: United States Democrats require a net gain of four seats in November midterm elections to wrest Senate control from Republicans who hold a 53-47 majority. Intensified by voter discontent over inflation, trade tariffs, and the war on Iran, tight races in states like Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, and Maine could determine the balance of power in Washington.
articles.description: From Texas to Maine, rising prices and the Iran war put key Senate races in play as Democrats fight for control.

articles.headline: United Nations Security Council rejects rival US and Russian resolutions
articles.title: Rival US and Russian resolutions on Western Sahara fail at UN
articles.summary: The United Nations Security Council failed to adopt competing United States and Russian resolutions regarding Western Sahara, casting uncertainty on the future of the peacekeeping mission known as MINURSO. Russia vetoed the US-backed proposal on Friday, while a rival Russian draft failed to garner the necessary nine votes before the mission mandate expired.
articles.description: UN Security Council rejected the competing proposals, leaving the peacekeeping mission without an approved extension.

articles.headline: Evacuation corridor opens in Russian-occupied Oleshky under a temporary ceasefire
articles.title: Hundreds evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during rare Ukraine ceasefire
articles.summary: The evacuation of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky is under way following a ceasefire brokered by United States First Lady Melania Trump. Residents wishing to leave have a four-hour window using a convoy of twenty-five buses organised by Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova. The temporary truce is scheduled to remain in effect until the end of November 1, 2026, providing the first pause in fighting in the Kherson region since February 2022.
articles.description: Hundreds of people are also understood to have stayed in the front-line town, despite the dangers.

articles.headline: Russia-Ukraine war devastation causes massive dolphin deaths in the Black Sea
articles.title: Dead dolphins, naval mines: Russia-Ukraine war destroys the Black Sea
articles.summary: Hostilities from the Russia-Ukraine conflict have severely impacted marine life, causing the deaths of over 120,000 cetaceans in the Black Sea by 2026. According to Ivan Rusev of Tuzly Lagoons national park, military sonar systems, explosions, and pollution from damaged warships disorient dolphins, impairing their echolocation and causing self-poisoning and fatal infections. Environmental degradation also threatens birds and fish populations, with cetacean recovery estimated to require up to fifty years.
articles.description: Conflict devastates Black Sea marine life, killing more than 120,000 dolphins and causing ecological damage.

articles.headline: Nations agree on biodiversity pact at the COP17 summit in Armenia
articles.title: Nations commit to get nature goals back on track at UN nature summit
articles.summary: Nearly 200 nations approved key texts at the COP17 biodiversity summit in Yerevan, Armenia, aiming to revive goals of halting nature destruction by 2030. Despite reaching agreements on addressing harmful subsidies and conservation finance, delegates expressed disappointment over missed opportunities and political challenges regarding scientific evidence. Ecuador was selected to host the next biodiversity talks in 2028 after a secret vote.
articles.description: The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation

articles.headline: Donald Trump reinstates rallies in Kansas and Iowa ahead of midterms
articles.title: Trump backtracks on rallies in turbulent end to midterms campaign
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump reversed an earlier decision to reinstate two campaign rallies in Kansas and Iowa ahead of the midterm elections on November 3, 2026. Speaking in Daytona, Florida, the 80-year-old leader urged voters to support Republican candidates. Meanwhile, a record 47.9 million Americans have already voted, including Pope Leo XIV, who became the first pontiff to cast a ballot in a political election.
articles.description: The U.S. President reinstated two rallies in Kansas and Iowa a day after cancelling them, saying Republicans “have a shot” in the midterms as a record 47.9 million Americans have already voted

articles.headline: New York governor signs legislation restricting artificial intelligence chatbot interactions with minors
articles.title: New York restricts AI chatbot interactions with children | Explained
articles.summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed two bills on October 28, 2026, designed to protect children from the risks posed by artificial intelligence chatbots and internet-connected baby monitors. The legislation bans artificial intelligence chatbots from engaging in harmful activities such as simulating romantic relationships or encouraging self-harm among minors.
