articles.headline: Narendra Modi inaugurates tourism and infrastructure projects in Ekta Nagar
articles.title: Modi says Opposition has become destructive force; calls for unity
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated twenty-three development projects worth 307.83 crore rupees and laid foundation stones for eight others in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, on October 31, 2026. The initiatives aim to upgrade visitor facilities and civic infrastructure around the Statue of Unity. The program coincided with Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, marking the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
articles.description: The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for eight development projects worth ₹118.88 crore, taking the total outlay for the 31 projects to ₹426.71 crore

articles.headline: Brighton defeats Manchester City to close Premier League gap
articles.title: Brighton shock Man City, closing gap on Premier League leader to two points
articles.summary: Brighton secured a 1-0 victory over Manchester City in the Premier League thanks to an early goal by Yasin Ayari and inspired goalkeeping by Bart Verbruggen. The result moves third-placed Brighton within two points of the leaders, handing manager Fabian Hurzeler's team a historic away win at City.
articles.description: Yasin Ayari goal hands third-placed Brighton 1-0 win at Manchester City, with two points separating top three in EPL.

articles.headline: Uttarakhand mandates co-pilots on Char Dham chartered flights
articles.title: Uttarakhand makes co-pilots mandatory on Char Dham chartered flights after crash killed six
articles.summary: Following a fatal helicopter crash in Joshimath, the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) made two-pilot crew configurations mandatory for pilgrimage charter services starting November 2. UCADA Chief Executive Officer Prateek Jain stated that pilots must also submit post-flight weather reports and obtain prior approval for take-offs and landings.
articles.description: The Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority has also made it compulsory for all pilots to submit a report to the authorities after every flight, detailing weather conditions and other important operational information

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Who will form Israel’s next government?
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Who will form Israel’s next government?
articles.description: Netanyahu and Eisenkot are locked in a struggle to form a governing coalition in the Knesset.

articles.headline: State government sanctions special funds for drinking water amid El Nino
articles.title: Govt. sanctions special funds for alternative drinking water sources amid El Nino concerns
articles.summary: The state government approved Rs 120 crore for alternative drinking water arrangements linked to the Singur reservoir and Rs 1 crore each for other districts to counter potential El Nino shortages. Panchayat Raj and Rural Water Supply Minister Danasari Anasuya Seethakka instructed officials to map vulnerable villages, secure local water sources, and expedite groundwater recharge works.

articles.headline: Pakistan defeats Sri Lanka by three wickets in tri-series final
articles.title: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka as Zaman’s century turns thrilling tri-series final
articles.summary: Opener Fakhar Zaman scored 127 runs to lead Pakistan to a three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the one-day international tri-series final at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. Pakistan successfully chased a target of 325, reaching 331-7 in 48.3 overs with contributions from Arafat Minhas and Saad Baig after Kamindu Mendis had earlier hit an unbeaten century for Sri Lanka.
articles.description: Fakhar Zaman's century outdoes Kamindu Mendis and propels Pakistan to three-wicket win against Sri Lanka in cricket final.

articles.headline: Democratic healthcare professionals surge as candidates in the midterm elections
articles.title: A cure for Trump? Why Democratic doctors are running in the 2026 midterms
articles.summary: Public health workers and physicians across the United States are increasingly running for congressional seats in the midterm elections. Experts attribute this political mobilization partly to voter frustration with rising medical expenses and the healthcare policies promoted by Republican President Donald Trump. Healthcare remains a prominent voting issue, underscored by a Pew Research Center poll showing strong voter concern.
articles.description: Democratic doctors aim to convert the backlash against the Trump administration’s health policies into midterm votes.

articles.headline: Dakar prepares to host the 2026 Youth Olympic Games
articles.title: Dakar Youth Olympics: Who gets to hold the flame?
articles.summary: Senegal is welcoming approximately 2,700 athletes, coaches, and supporters for the 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening in Dakar. International Olympic Committee leader Kirsty Coventry described the event as an opportunity for Africa to demonstrate its capabilities despite the nation facing financial and political challenges. The competitions feature diverse teenage athletes, though geopolitical tensions have already emerged regarding national representations.
articles.description: Senegal makes history by becoming the first African country to host an Olympic event.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate arrests four individuals in cross-border drug network probe
articles.title: ED arrests four more accused, including Myanmar national, in cross-border drug network
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate took four suspects into custody, including Myanmar national Thangcintuang, as part of an ongoing investigation into an international narco-hawala network. Following raids conducted under Operation Trident across Assam, Mizoram, and Manipur, the agency uncovered extensive financial records detailing currency exchanges and payments made in kind to drug suppliers located in Myanmar.
articles.description: Chintuang was a Myanmar-based supplier of the 49.1 kg methamphetamine consignment seized in August 2025, while Lalrammuana was the main handler and Jabrul Haque its intended receiver at Damchhera-Kanhmun border; Abu Saleh was allegedly the operator whose account received ₹11.44 crore

articles.headline: France deploys 70,000 security personnel as youth protests spread across Europe
articles.title: Clashes break out between police and protesters in Paris
articles.summary: France deployed 70,000 police and gendarmes on October 31, 2026, for a third weekend of protests over living costs and education. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of high disorder risks after dark. Authorities restricted march routes and imposed curfews. Meanwhile, youth demonstrations and TikTok-driven rallies also spread to Germany, Spain, Italy, and other European nations, with organizers reporting high participation.
articles.description: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween

articles.headline: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar arrives in Atlanta for G20 meeting
articles.title: External Affairs Minister Jaishankar in U.S. for G20 Foreign Ministers’ meet
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar arrived in Atlanta on Thursday to attend the G20 Foreign Ministers meeting chaired by United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The two-day discussions focus on global energy supply chains and security challenges ahead of the December leaders summit in Miami. Following these sessions, Jaishankar will travel to Antigua and Barbuda for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.
articles.description: The External Affairs Minister will participate in the two-day deliberations, which will begin with Mr. Rubio’s address on geopolitical issues

articles.headline: Oleshky evacuees reunite with families in northern Ukraine following ceasefire
articles.title: Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees
articles.summary: Displaced residents from the occupied city of Oleshky met relatives at a designated site in the Chernihiv region after crossing the border from Belarus. The relocations followed a temporary truce brokered by United States First Lady Melania Trump that commenced across the Kherson frontline on Tuesday. Buses and ambulances transported the individuals who had previously journeyed through Crimea and Russia. The cessation of hostilities is scheduled to conclude on Sunday 1 November, according to BBC correspondent Dan Johnson reporting from the northern border.
articles.description: The BBC's Dan Johnson travelled to the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus after evacuated Oleshky residents arrived in buses and ambulances following a temporary ceasefire.

articles.headline: Police in Hyderabad rescue 43 women and arrest eight suspects in illegal egg harvesting racket
articles.title: 43 women rescued in illegal human egg harvesting racket in Hyderabad
articles.summary: Begumpet and Saroornagar police rescued 43 women and arrested eight suspects during simultaneous raids at four premises in Hyderabad. Authorities busted an alleged commercial egg harvesting racket that recruited women from various states by offering monetary incentives. Police seized documents, mobile phones, and medical supplies while investigating compliance under the Assisted Reproductive Technology Act.
articles.description: Police examine alleged recruitment of women across States, suspected use of rented premises and links with fertility centres and ART banks in Hyderabad

articles.headline: Pakistan Prime Minister orders accelerated federal development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan region
articles.title: Pakistan PM orders fast-tracking of development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan
articles.summary: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed officials to accelerate ongoing federal development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan and ensure the timely release of funds during a meeting in Islamabad. The region is a key component of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor passing through territory claimed by India. Officials reviewed progress on hydropower, infrastructure, and solar energy projects during the session.
articles.description: The development assumes significance for India as Gilgit-Baltistan is illegally and forcibly occupied by Pakistan

articles.headline: Scientists use epigenetic control to silence hepatitis B viral DNA
articles.title: Gene therapy offers to beat hepatitis B virus by muting its DNA
articles.summary: Researchers have developed an experimental therapy called CRMA-1001 that successfully silences hepatitis B virus DNA in mice by selectively adding methylation marks without altering host genes. According to a study published on September 21 in Nature Biomedical Engineering, the technique utilizes CRISPR-Cas9 to deliver the silencing machinery, offering a promising path toward a lasting functional cure by preventing viral rebound.
articles.description: An experimental therapy called CRMA-1001 is a remarkable development because, instead of targeting the virus directly, it silences the viral DNA; this is promising because current treatments rarely eliminate the DNA, which allows the virus to rebound

articles.headline: United Nations political mission in Somalia concludes operations after three decades
articles.title: UN ends its Somalia political mission after three decades
articles.summary: The United Nations political mission in Somalia officially concluded operations after a two-year transition period, ending over three decades of peacebuilding efforts in the nation. Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud previously requested the termination of the mandate. The transition occurs as the government continues its fight against Al-Shabaab amid international funding cuts and upcoming elections scheduled for May.
articles.description: UNSOM was established by the UN Security Council in 2013 to support Somali authorities in the transition to democracy and the rule of law after more than two decades of conflict involving militias, Islamist groups and criminal gangs

articles.headline: Two students injured after classroom ceiling collapses in Khammam district
articles.title: Two students injured as concrete layer falls from classroom ceiling in State-run Gurukul in Khammam district
articles.summary: Two ninth-grade students sustained injuries when a concrete layer from their classroom ceiling fell on them while attending class at a State-run Gurukul in Bonakal mandal headquarters town. The victims received initial treatment at a local Primary Health Centre before being transferred to the Government General Hospital in Khammam. Both are currently reported to be out of danger, while student union leaders demand structural inspections.

articles.headline: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado urges 2027 elections
articles.title: Venezuela’s Machado lauds Trump for ‘freedom’, urges 2027 elections
articles.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado thanked United States President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Thursday for opening freedom through the January abduction of President Nicolas Maduro. Speaking in Caracas after returning from exile, Machado called for presidential elections to be held in 2027 while criticizing a recent controversial oil agreement finalized by interim leader Delcy Rodriguez.
articles.description: Nobel winner returns to Venezuela from exile, urging elections and criticising a controversial US oil deal with Caracas.

articles.headline: Federal judge blocks Trump administration Medicaid work exemption rules
articles.title: US judge blocks Trump’s Medicaid rule forcing ill to prove impairment
articles.summary: United States District Judge Richard Stearns blocked a Trump administration rule on Thursday requiring chronically ill Medicaid enrollees to prove they are medically frail to qualify for work exemptions. Siding with twenty-five states and the District of Columbia, Stearns ruled that the stricter criteria unlawfully restricted care access. Meanwhile, broader work requirements taking effect January 2027 remain unchanged.
articles.description: A US district judge sided with 25 states and the District of Columbia, which sued the administration.

articles.headline: Telangana government sets maximum retail prices for three fine rice varieties
articles.title: Telangana govt. announces maximum retail price of three fine rice varieties between ₹66 and ₹79 per kg
articles.summary: The Telangana government established price caps for high-demand fine rice varieties in Hyderabad and Medchal following discussions with wholesalers and retailers. The new maximum retail prices per kilogram are set at sixty-six rupees for BPT and KNM, seventy-four rupees for RNR and Telangana Sona, and seventy-nine rupees for HMT and JSR varieties. Officials warned that violations will face strict enforcement actions from the Civil Supplies department.

articles.headline: SEBI chairman says market regulator monitors governance developments at Tata Group
articles.title: SEBI chairman says market regulator keeping eye on Tata Group developments
articles.summary: Securities and Exchange Board of India Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey stated that the market regulator is actively observing governance developments involving the holding company level of the Tata Group. Speaking in Mumbai, Pandey emphasized that the conglomerate's twenty-six publicly listed companies and their promoters remain fully subject to standard disclosure and compliance regulations. The remarks followed ongoing discussions regarding governance matters and proposed listings at Tata Sons.
articles.description: The comments came amid differences over governance matters at Tata Sons

articles.headline: India outlines artificial intelligence and maritime security priorities for UN seat
articles.title: India says AI, maritime security key priorities for its UNSC candidature for 2028–29
articles.summary: India has identified artificial intelligence and maritime security as core priorities for its upcoming United Nations Security Council candidature for the 2028-2029 term. Permanent Representative Harish Parvathaneni stated during a New York debate that technology must reinforce maritime safety and commerce without deepening global disparities. Elections for the sole Asia-Pacific Group seat are scheduled to occur in June.
articles.description: Mr. Parvathaneni underscored the need to safeguard freedom of navigation and maritime commerce, saying recent attacks against commercial shipping have demonstrated how disruptions at critical maritime chokepoints can have consequences far beyond their immediate geography

articles.headline: Thousands of protesters gather across German cities amid student demonstrations
articles.title: Thousands rally in Berlin as Gen Z protests in more than 30 German cities
articles.summary: Thousands of demonstrators assembled in Berlin and over thirty other German locations during a wave of nationwide student protests organized by the Gen Z Regelt alliance. Participants voiced strong opposition against government education funding cuts, rising living costs, and military spending. While most demonstrations remained calm, scuffles occurred in Cologne as police moved to contain a march during the coordinated events.
articles.description: Demonstrations sweeping Europe are inspiring young Germans frustrated by rising costs of living amid military spending.

articles.headline: Iran rules out bilateral meetings with United States despite rising tensions
articles.title: Iran has no plans for talks with U.S.: Foreign Minister
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Tehran has no ongoing plans for direct meetings with American officials despite growing concerns regarding a return to armed conflict. Speaking to Al Jazeera and cited by the state news agency IRNA, Araghchi confirmed that Iran received and reviewed a written message from United States Vice President J.D. Vance. He cautioned that Washington must avoid sowing discord while noting that diplomatic consultations continue through regional mediators.
articles.description: Araghchi confirmed that Iran received a letter from U.S. Vice President J. D. Vance, following days of diplomatic efforts to head off a return to violence

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate detains Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan outside jail
articles.title: ED detains SP leader Azam Khan from outside Rampur jail as soon as he comes out on bail
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate detained seventy-eight-year-old Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan from outside the Rampur jail in Uttar Pradesh immediately following his release on bail on October 31, 2026. Officials indicated he may face imminent arrest under money laundering legislation. The Allahabad High Court had previously suspended his sentence in a dual PAN card fraud case alongside his son Abdullah Azam Khan.
articles.description: On October 29, the Allahabad High Court suspended the sentence of Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam Khan in the alleged dual PAN card case and granted them bail.

articles.headline: Bangladesh opposition leader warns against transit corridor and seeks fair Ganges pact
articles.title: Bangladesh opposition leader warns against India corridor, seeks fair Ganges water pact: Reports
articles.summary: National Citizen Party convener Nahid Islam criticised the administration led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at a Dhaka rally on October 30, 2026. He warned against facilitating an Indian transit corridor and demanded the renewal of the bilateral Ganges Water-Sharing Treaty before its expiration on December 12, 2026, threatening public protests if Bangladesh fails to secure its fair water share.
articles.description: In the rally, the NCP leader also accused Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's government of seeking to facilitate an Indian transit corridor through the country

articles.headline: Bharatiya Janata Party criticises opposition INDIA bloc over mock Parliament session
articles.title: ‘Make Rahul Gandhi a mock PM’: BJP slams INDIA bloc over mock Parliament
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party condemned the opposition INDIA alliance on October 31, 2026, for holding a mock Parliament session to symbolically impeach Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral roll irregularities. At a press conference, BJP leaders defended the special intensive revision process, rejected claims of stolen votes, and argued that poverty reduction proves the government's efficacy.
articles.description: Rejecting Opposition’s ‘vote chori’ allegations, BJP MP Sambit Patra says SIR had been conducted 10 times during Congress rule and accused the party of double standards

articles.headline: Investigators suspect electrical power leakage from pool lights in Conrad hotel incident
articles.title: Preliminary reports suspect power leakage into pool from wiring for lights inside pool
articles.summary: Investigators examining the Conrad hotel swimming pool following a fatal incident on October 31, 2026, suspect that a short circuit in the wiring of the underwater lights caused power to leak into the water. Scene of Crime officers detected electric jolts during their inspection. The tragedy, which resulted in two deaths, prompted the hotel to close the facility for maintenance through November 30, 2026.
articles.description: Karnataka Swimming Association calls for a Swimming Pools Act to ensure safety norms and quality guidelines

articles.headline: Indian women cricket coach Amol Muzumdar praises team health and emerging talent
articles.title: Indian women’s cricket in a healthy state: Muzumdar
articles.summary: Indian women cricket head coach Amol Muzumdar stated on October 31, 2026, that the national team could soon adopt a specialist T20I squad structure similar to the men's team. Speaking at a Sports Journalists Association of Mumbai event, he commended the exceptional talent observed at the Centre of Excellence camps and praised outgoing captain Harmanpreet Kaur as leadership transitions to Smriti Mandhana.
articles.description: The head coach feels the next generation is ready to excel in the T20 format

articles.headline: Polish President Nawrocki accuses Prime Minister Tusk of court takeover
articles.title: Poland's President accuses PM Tusk of forced takeover of country's top court
articles.summary: Polish President Karol Nawrocki accused Prime Minister Donald Tusk of staging a forced takeover of the Constitutional Tribunal after suspended president Bogdan Swieczkowski was replaced by Anna Korwin-Piotrowska on October 30, 2026. The suspension escalated a long-running political dispute between the nationalist president and the pro-European government over the judiciary. Nawrocki called for urgent political consultations while protesters gathered outside the court.
articles.description: A long-running political dispute over the Constitutional Tribunal has effectively paralysed the institution, with the pro-European government and the nationalist President refusing to ‌recognise appointees put forward by the other side

articles.headline: National Conference downplays meeting of seventeen disgruntled legislators
articles.title: ‘Internal democracy’, not ‘rebellion’, NC says of 17 MLAs meeting over party affairs
articles.summary: Seventeen disgruntled National Conference legislators forwarded a list of demands to party president Farooq Abdullah on October 31, 2026, after holding a meeting in Srinagar. Provincial president Showkat Ahmad Mir downplayed the gathering as internal democracy rather than a rebellion. The demands included intensifying the struggle for statehood, fulfilling 2024 manifesto promises, and reconsidering cabinet portfolios and advisor appointments.
articles.description: The list of demands sent to Dr. Abdullah urged “intensifying of struggle for restoration of Statehood, implementation of the promises made in the 2024 manifesto within six months, removing CM’s advisor Wani, and reconsidering portfolios assigned to Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary”.

articles.headline: Netanyahu's party claims election stolen as bloc loses parliament majority
articles.title: Netanyahu's party claims Israel election 'stolen' as results show him losing majority
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party amplified allegations that Arab-led parties stole the election with foreign assistance after final results released on October 29, 2026, showed his bloc winning 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset. Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg asked the Shin Bet to investigate suspected foreign interference. Opponents accused Mr. Netanyahu of delegitimising the vote to block potential coalitions.
articles.description: Israeli media reported that members of Mr. Netanyahu's party were accusing Qatar — a country that many Israelis view as a patron of Hamas, the Gaza-based militant group

articles.headline: South Africa defeats Australia to win Test series
articles.title: South Africa hammer Australia as Harmer takes career best bowling of 6-16
articles.summary: South Africa defeated Australia by 176 runs in the third Test at Newlands on October 31, 2026, securing a 2-1 series victory and claiming the number one spot in the world rankings. Australia was bowled out for 111 while chasing 288, hampered by spinner Simon Harmer taking career-best figures of 6-16 in the innings and 10-120 in the match.
articles.description: Simon Harmer picked a career-best 6-16 as South Africa beat Australia by 176 runs to clinch Test series 2-1.

articles.headline: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un calls for rapid drone technology expansion
articles.title: North Korea's Kim calls for rapid expansion of drone technology, observes testing of weapons
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected an unmanned aeronautical technology exhibition and observed weapons testing on October 29, 2026, according to state media reports. Emphasizing the need for absolute superiority in drone warfare, the leader sought to strengthen conventional and nuclear capabilities amid ongoing border tensions with South Korea. Experts noted that troops deployed to Russia likely gained critical battlefield expertise.
articles.description: In a speech at the exhibition, Mr. Kim stressed the need to seize “the absolute superiority in the drone technology” and announced unspecified steps needed to “rapidly expand and strengthen the unmanned aeronautical technology,” says Korean Central News Agency

articles.headline: China expels record 33 members from Communist Party during annual plenum
articles.title: Record number of purges as Xi emphasises 'party discipline' at China political gathering
articles.summary: China has expelled a record thirty-three members from the Communist Party during its annual plenum in Beijing, which concluded on Thursday. Sixteen of those removed are from the military, including former generals Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli. According to analysts, the sweeping anti-corruption purges aim to consolidate political authority ahead of the next Party Congress.
articles.description: Xi's anti-corruption campaign has become "an effort to consolidate and maintain authority", observers say.

articles.headline: Hundreds in Kolkata march in protest against recent bookstall attacks
articles.title: ‘Walk for books’: Hundreds march in Kolkata against attack on bookstalls
articles.summary: Hundreds of citizens, activists, and politicians participated in a rally on College Street in Kolkata on Saturday to protest recent vandalism targeting local bookstalls. Organised without political banners, the march followed the destruction of at least 292 stalls during Durga Puja festivities. While right-wing groups and the Bharatiya Janata Party were blamed, the BJP denied involvement as participants carried books and demanded the protection of education.
articles.description: Citizens, activists, professors, and politicians join the march, which was held without any political banner. It was organised in protest against attacks on bookstalls during Durga Puja, blamed on right-wing groups and the BJP

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh explores solar powered electric vehicle charging station challenges
articles.title: Solar power charging taking baby steps in A.P. despite better conditions
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh faces high upfront costs and infrastructure hurdles in developing solar-powered electric vehicle charging stations, according to industry experts and officials. While Convergence Energy Services Limited and Tata Power operate conventional chargers in the state, solar adoption remains limited due to expensive land requirements and transmission costs. State Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar noted that officials are currently evaluating these operational challenges to protect farmers' interests.
articles.description: The State has the perfect sunny conditions to launch solar-powered EV charging stations, but the industry is still in its early stages. It is still facing challenges in the form of high upfront investment and uncertain returns; the State government is aggressively developing EV charging stations, but not the solar-powered ones, says Minister

articles.headline: Radico Khaitan establishes Scotland subsidiary to secure malt whisky supplies
articles.title: Radico Khaitan sets sights on Scotland to secure malt whisky supplies
articles.summary: Indian spirits manufacturer Radico Khaitan Limited has incorporated a Scotland-based subsidiary to evaluate opportunities in whisky distillation, maturation, and trading. Managing Director Abhishek Khaitan stated the initiative aims to strengthen the company's malt whisky supply chain without altering the Indian provenance of its Rampur single malt. The expansion aligns with efforts to diversify export markets following disruptions in the West Asia and Gulf corridor.
articles.description: Recent disruptions in the West Asia and Gulf corridor highlighted the risks of concentration in individual markets. The company was working to strengthen distribution across other regions.

articles.headline: Democrats threaten Republican control of the US Senate ahead of midterm elections
articles.title: Republicans defend their bastions, as senate comes within reach of Democrats
articles.summary: As the United States approaches midterm elections, forecasts indicate that the Republican Party majority in the Senate is under threat from Democrats. The party currently holds a 53 to 47 majority with thirty-five seats contested this year, including seven toss-up seats identified by the Cook Political Report across several states according to reports published on October twenty-ninth, 2026.
articles.description: The GOP has a 53–47 majority in the Senate currently, with 35 seats being contested this year. Of these, seven are “toss ups”, according to a non-partisan election analyser. These seats are in Iowa, Arkansas, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas. All of these – except Michigan – are seats which are currently held by Republicans

articles.headline: Tribal collective demands comprehensive study into infant deaths in Attappady
articles.title: Tribal collective seeks wider study into infant deaths in Keralam’s Attappady
articles.summary: The Thampu tribal collective urged the Kerala government to address socioeconomic causes of infant deaths after 124 children died between 2012 and 2026. Representatives met Health Minister K. Muraleedharan on October 31, 2026, seeking a two-phase action plan, land rights under the Forest Rights Act, mobile ration shops, and better healthcare delivery to tackle recurring issues like low birth weight and malnutrition.
articles.description: A delegation of the tribal collective, Thampu, meets Health Minister K. Muraleedharan and calls for a new approach that addresses the social, cultural and economic factors behind the deaths, along with enhanced health-care measures

articles.headline: Karnataka rural population projected to decline to thirty percent by 2047
articles.title: Rural share of Karnataka population to fall to 30% by 2047
articles.summary: Karnataka expects its overall population to grow from 6.9 crore to 7.9 crore by 2047, while the rural share falls from 52.17% to 30%. According to the Karnataka State Regional Urbanisation Plan-2047 report published on October 31, 2026, the state will invest ₹5 lakh crore across seven regional growth nodes led by Bengaluru and Mysuru to manage urbanisation and migration.
articles.description: The rural population is expected to decline from the current 3.6 crore to 2.4 crore by 2047, according to the Karnataka State Regional Urbanisation Plan-2047 report

articles.headline: Netanyahu attacks Israel’s Arab parties as he falls short of majority
articles.title: Netanyahu attacks Israel’s Arab parties as he falls short of majority
articles.description: Israel’s Prime Minister accused Palestinian-Israeli parties of election fraud.

articles.headline: Four-year-old boy dies in stray dog attack in Kalaburagi
articles.title: Four-year-old boy dies in stray dog attack; 13 others injured in Kalaburagi
articles.summary: A four-year-old boy named Manoj died from severe injuries after a stray dog attacked him on October 30, 2026, in Kalaburagi. Thirteen other people sustained bite injuries from the suspected rabid dog during their morning walk the next day. All injured victims received treatment at the District Hospital, prompting angry residents to demand civic action and compensation.

articles.headline: Ethiopian prime minister puts cabinet ministers through military training
articles.title: Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training
articles.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed directed cabinet ministers and senior officials, including Finance Minister Fitsum Assefa and Health Minister Mekdes Daba, through military exercises at the Hurso military training centre. The prime minister stated on social media that armed forces discipline builds stronger leadership, amid ongoing domestic security challenges in regions like Tigray and tensions with neighbouring Eritrea.
articles.description: The prime minister has previously emphasised military preparedness as central to his government's ambitions.

articles.headline: Elon Musk plans massive merger between SpaceX and Tesla
articles.title: Merging SpaceX, Tesla makes more sense for Musk than its investors
articles.summary: American billionaire Elon Musk is pursuing a corporate combination of his aerospace firm and electric vehicle manufacturer to create an integrated artificial intelligence and industrial conglomerate valued at three point five trillion dollars. Industry analysts note that the proposed union could eliminate internal checks on capital allocation and strengthen control over critical technological infrastructure.

articles.headline: Syria weighs joining regional defence pact with Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan
articles.title: Syria considering entry into Mecca defence pact, says foreign minister
articles.summary: Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani announced that his government is evaluating potential entry into the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement. Signed in August by Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan, the pact treats an attack on one member as an assault on all three. Al-Shaibani made the announcement at the Manama Dialogue conference in Bahrain, noting Damascus strongly supports regional stability.
articles.description: Damascus 'evaluating' whether to join the alliance that binds Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

articles.headline: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham open to slavery apology but rejects reparations
articles.title: Britain open to apologising for slavery, says U.K. PM Andy Burnham
articles.summary: United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated on October 30, 2026, that his government is open to formally apologising for Britain's historical role in the slave trade ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting. While ruling out financial reparations, Burnham announced a debt restructuring initiative led by former Prime Minister Gordon Brown to support impoverished Commonwealth nations.
articles.description: Mr. Burnham pushed back against the notion of financial reparations for victims of slavery saying that the British people could not be held responsible for historical wrongs; Burnham’s omission of colonialism ‘inexcusable’, said Tharoor

articles.headline: EKA Mobility plans ₹1,000-crore R&D investment to expand manufacturing capacity
articles.title: EKA Mobility plans ₹1,000-crore R&D investment, targets 40,000-unit capacity utilisation by 2030
articles.summary: Electric commercial vehicle manufacturer EKA Mobility announced plans to invest ₹1,000 crore in research and development over four to five years. Founder and chairman Sudhir Mehta stated the Pune-based firm inaugurated six new plants, raising annual production capacity to 40,000 vehicles. The company aims to scale domestic sales and increase exports to African markets, while navigating financing constraints.
articles.description: EKA aims to raise exports to 20-30% of total sales over the next few years. It is exploring further opportunities in the African markets.

articles.headline: BJP booth agent files voter deletion forms against Muslim residents in Delhi
articles.title: In Delhi, BJP booth agents file deletion forms against Muslim voters living at their addresses
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party booth-level agent Chandra Shekhar Nainwal filed Form 7 applications to remove twenty-eight voters from the electoral roll in Dayalpur, Delhi, citing reasons such as permanent shifting or death. Resident Sajid Hussain discovered on October 28, 2026, that deletion forms targeted his family members. The incident occurred during the ongoing special intensive revision claims and objections period, as recorded by the Election Commission of India.
articles.description: BJP BLAs submit nearly 68% of Form 7s seeking deletions as ‘objector’ in Mustafabad, all against Muslim electors citing ‘absent/permanently shifted’ or ‘death’

articles.headline: Pranos Fusion aims to finalise design for India's first private tokamak in 2027
articles.title: India’s first fusion power company takes key steps
articles.summary: Bengaluru-based startup Pranos Fusion expects to finalise the blueprint for its PRANIK nuclear fusion reactor in 2027. Co-founder and CEO Shaurya Kaushal explained that the company built a smaller tokamak named PRAGYA to test plasma control and superconducting magnets. Incubated at the Institute of Plasma Research, the firm aims to advance clean energy technology without radioactive uranium.
articles.description: Designs for the first privately built tokamak, a nuclear reactor that uses fusion to produce energy, could be firmed up in 2027 by Bengaluru-based startup Pranos Fusion

articles.headline: Maharashtra passes Women Farmers' Empowerment Bill to grant independent recognition
articles.title: Towards recognising women farmers
articles.summary: Maharashtra passed the Women Farmers' Empowerment Bill in July 2026, introducing Woman Farmer Certificates to grant independent legal recognition regardless of land ownership. The legislation implements the activity-based definition proposed in the 2007 National Policy for Farmers. This milestone concludes decades of advocacy by civil society organisations to combat systemic invisibility in agriculture.
articles.description: Maharashtra’s passage of the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, brings into focus the structural bias against the female agricultural workforce, highlights the need for a database of women farmers and using it to ensure access to welfare schemes

articles.headline: Spacecraft rely on atmospheric drag and parachutes to reduce velocity during landing
articles.title: The science of Gaganyaan parachutes | Explained
articles.summary: Spacecraft entering the earth's atmosphere primarily use atmospheric drag to reduce velocity through aerobraking during descent. Towards the terminal phase, additional decelerating systems such as parachutes must be deployed to ensure a gentle touchdown on land or in the sea by lowering speed to acceptable limits for safe recovery.
articles.description: Why does Gaganyaan need multiple parachutes? How are they tested?

articles.headline: Early voting turnout surges past forty-three million in United States midterms
articles.title: More than 43 million ballots cast so far in midterms early voting surge
articles.summary: More than 43 million Americans have cast early ballots ahead of the United States midterm elections that will determine control of Congress. According to University of Florida Election Lab data released on October 30, 2026, daily voting rates have averaged four to five million, with Texas and Hispanic communities showing exceptionally high turnout compared with previous election cycles.
articles.description: Hispanic voters have helped drive the early voting numbers, which appear to outpace overall turnout for previous elections in some battleground counties.

articles.headline: NTPC reports 14% rise in net profit for September quarter
articles.title: NTPC Q2 net up 14% to ₹5,320-cr. on higher generation, improved efficiencies
articles.summary: State-owned power producer NTPC Ltd. reported that its standalone net profit rose 14.3% year-on-year to ₹5,320 crore in the September quarter, driven by higher electricity generation and improved operational efficiencies. According to the company, commercial generation increased 11.1% to 92.413 billion units, while plant load factor improved to 73.53%. Revenue from operations also increased nearly 17% to ₹45,752 crore during the period.
articles.description: The company’s commercial generation increased 11.1% YoY to 92.413 billion units (BU).

articles.headline: Sámi communities face border restrictions between Norway and Russia
articles.title: On the Norway-Russia border, the Sámi people face a growing divide
articles.summary: Indigenous Sámi communities along the Norway-Russia border face growing administrative divides and heightened security measures following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. According to local residents like Nils Boine, traditional cross-border travel, shopping trips, and social connections have stalled due to safety concerns and stricter regulations, impacting regional tourism and cross-border lifestyles in Finnmark.
articles.description: As Russia’s war in Ukraine reshapes this Arctic frontier, Sámi communities struggle to sustain cross-border traditions.

articles.headline: Aging NASA telescope set to reenter Earth atmosphere following failed rescue
articles.title: NASA telescope on verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
articles.summary: A 1.5-ton NASA telescope is projected to plunge back to Earth on or around October 30, 2026, after a robotic rescue mission failed earlier this year. Launched in November 2004, the Swift Observatory operated for 22 years before intense solar activity dragged it down. Mission officials state that while most of the structure will burn up upon reentry, durable components could reach the surface within a designated global zone.
articles.description: Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission's chief scientist

articles.headline: Displaced Sudanese artists preserve cultural heritage amid ongoing civil war
articles.title: Studios destroyed, traditions saved: Artists fight to save Sudan’s culture
articles.summary: Displaced Sudanese artists and cultural professionals who fled conflict in Khartoum and other regions are utilizing art and music in Port Sudan to preserve local traditions and foster social cohesion. Organizations including UNESCO and local writers unions have established shelters and supported initiatives for affected individuals. Although the ongoing war has severely impacted the cultural sector and left many without workspaces, participants continue community programs aimed at countering division.
articles.description: Artists in Sudan are working to save culture and traditions amid the country's war.

articles.headline: Alaska Senate race triggers federal investigation over alleged ballot stacking
articles.title: Alaska’s two ‘Dan Sullivans’: How common is ballot stacking, does it work?
articles.summary: A political controversy has emerged in Alaska regarding allegations that Democratic aides recruited a namesake candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan to siphon votes from the Republican incumbent in the United States Senate election. President Donald Trump ordered a Justice Department investigation into the matter, while Democratic Senator Mary Peltola denied any involvement in the scheme. Legal experts note that similar voter manipulation tactics have occasionally influenced previous American elections.
articles.description: Same names on Alaska ballot triggered political firestorm in US, prompting a Justice Department investigation.

articles.headline: Iran says missing fishermen found following alleged United States attack
articles.title: Iran says fishermen found after accusing U.S. of attack in Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran reported on October 31, 2026, that two missing fishermen from Qeshm had been found following what state television described as an American attack on their fishing vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. Earlier reports indicated two other fishermen were wounded in the incident. Agence France-Presse contacted the United States Central Command for comment on the allegations.
articles.description: Two fishermen from Qeshm, who had gone missing following an attack by the American enemy on their fishing boat this morning, have been found, state television said

articles.headline: Binance freezes billions in crypto funds following potential security issue
articles.title: Binance says $6.3bn stolen in biggest crypto heist in history
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance suspended all deposits and withdrawals on Thursday after freezing at least $2.54bn due to a potential security issue. The world's largest exchange stated that user funds remained safe while security teams investigated alongside law enforcement. Founder Changpeng Zhao suggested the platform was targeted in a cyber heist, which caused Bitcoin prices to drop nearly five percent below $77,000 following the incident.
articles.description: A blockchain intelligence firm attributes the attack to North Korean state-sponsored hackers.

articles.headline: Former rebel leader elected chief minister of Philippine Muslim region
articles.title: Former rebel leader elected chief minister of Philippine Muslim region
articles.description: Former Muslim rebel leader Abdulraof Macacua has been elected chief minister of the Philippines' Bangsamoro region.

articles.headline: Serbia's victorious student movement demands sweeping dismissals in police and judiciary
articles.title: Student-backed election winners demand sweeping resignations in Serbia
articles.summary: Serbia's newly elected Student List movement has demanded the immediate dismissal of top police, intelligence, and judiciary officials following their electoral victory against former president Aleksandar Vučić's party. Meeting in Belgrade on Thursday, the novice politicians aim to prevent the destruction of evidence during the power handover. The movement emerged from protests over a fatal November 2024 railway station canopy collapse in Novi Sad that killed 16 people.
articles.description: Days after ousting Aleksandar Vučić's party from power, Student List MPs call for top figures to stand down.

articles.headline: Houthi forces claim six missile and drone attacks across Saudi Arabia
articles.title: Houthi forces claim six attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities
articles.summary: Iran-backed Houthi forces claimed responsibility for six missile and drone attacks targeting commercial and military infrastructure across Saudi Arabia on Thursday. The strikes hit locations including the Ras Tanura oil refinery and Riyadh airports, despite recent high-level diplomatic talks in Tehran. Saudi air defences intercepted two ballistic missiles, resulting in one civilian injury and minor property damage from falling shrapnel in Riyadh according to officials.
articles.description: The announcement comes despite talks between Iran and the Mecca pact countries in Tehran earlier this week.

articles.headline: Akhilesh Yadav questions Amit Shah over Uttar Pradesh crime
articles.title: Akhilesh Yadav questions Amit Shah over crimes against women, Dalits in U.P.
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav questioned Union Home Minister Amit Shah regarding crimes targeting women and Dalits in Uttar Pradesh. The inquiry followed Amit Shah's assertion that the Bharatiya Janata Party government remains firmly established in the state, while Samajwadi Party member Awadhesh Prasad argued that recent electoral defeats indicate the ruling party has lost political footing.
articles.description: Home Minister should look into why women face so much injustice in Uttar Pradesh, why the state witnesses so many murders and why people from the Dalit community are among the worst affected, Akhilesh Yadav said

articles.headline: Heavy pesticide use threatens Keralam cardamom ecosystem
articles.title: Heavy pesticide use puts Keralam’s cardamom ecosystem under pressure
articles.summary: Cardamom growers in Keralam are applying up to 24 pesticide rounds annually due to rising temperatures extending the crop harvest cycle and increasing pest activity. Experts warn that mixing multiple chemicals into single spray tanks can weaken plants, harm pollinators, and cause runoff in the Indian Cardamom Hills, prompting calls for targeted treatments and better farm management.
articles.description: As growers face a year-round harvest cycle driven by warming temperatures, they mix up to five or six different products, including insecticides, fungicides, micronutrients, and growth promoters, into a single tank. Experts warn that such ‘tank cocktails’ can actually weaken cardamom plants, increase their disease risk, harms essential pollinators.

articles.headline: United Nations closes political mission in Somalia after thirty years
articles.title: UN closes Somalia mission, ending three decades of political engagement
articles.summary: The United Nations concluded its political mission in Somalia on Saturday after a two-year transition requested by the government in Mogadishu, ending three decades of involvement. According to officials, responsibilities have been transferred to local institutions and international agencies, though the country continues to face severe security, humanitarian, and political challenges alongside shrinking foreign aid.
articles.description: Somalia hails the UN mission's closure as a milestone amid political tensions and cuts to international support.

articles.headline: Congress questions government over transparency regarding IDBI Bank sale
articles.title: Why do questions of transparency arise in every major deal under Modi government?: Congress on IDBI bank row
articles.summary: The Indian National Congress party raised transparency concerns on October 31, 2026, regarding the government's approval of selling a sixty percent stake in IDBI Bank to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings. Opposition leaders questioned potential conflicts of interest involving board members and a reduction in share price, while Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman defended the transaction and accused critics of spreading falsehoods.
articles.description: Jairam Ramesh claimed the recent investigations by Businessworld have brought to light significant revelations that raise serious questions regarding this decision by the Modi government

articles.headline: Odisha launches search operation for twelve missing landslide victims
articles.title: Search underway for 12 people missing in landslide-hit southern Odisha village
articles.summary: The Odisha government deployed one hundred seventy rescue personnel on October 31, 2026, to locate twelve missing people following a rain-triggered landslide at Gidipabali village. Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P. Patil stated that the disaster occurred during incessant rainfall from cyclone Arnab, which also caused fatalities across southern districts and displaced numerous residents to relief camps.
articles.description: Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P. Patil said altogether, 170 personnel of the National Disaster Response Force, Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force and Special Operation Group have been engaged in the operation to locate the missing people

articles.headline: Do tough laws deter drug crimes? Lessons from Singapore and Malaysia
articles.title: Do tough laws deter drug crimes? Lessons from Singapore and Malaysia
articles.description: As Malaysia rethinks the death penalty for drug offences, Singapore insists tough laws deter substance abuse.

articles.headline: Asian Champions Trophy highlights performance gap in men's hockey
articles.title: Asian Champions Trophy: 15 years on, a question of relevance and form
articles.summary: The men's Asian Champions Trophy reached its midpoint on October 31, 2026, highlighting a significant performance gap between the host nation India and competing teams. Observers noted that the tournament raises questions regarding the current relevance of the competition and the future trajectory of international hockey development across the Asian continent.
articles.description: While it was always expected that the host would dominate the proceedings this year, the huge gap on the turf raises questions about the relevance of the competition, especially for India

articles.headline: Riot police deploy outside Polish constitutional court amid leadership dispute
articles.title: Protests outside Poland’s constitutional court: What’s the crisis about?
articles.summary: Riot police secured the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw on Friday following a leadership dispute between Prime Minister Donald Tusk's administration and the nationalist opposition Law and Justice party. The confrontation escalated after judges suspended tribunal president Bogdan Swieczkowski, prompting President Karol Nawrocki to interrupt an official trip to Senegal and return to Poland for urgent consultations.
articles.description: Poland’s centrist government says it is restoring judicial independence after years of far-right political interference.

articles.headline: Thousands protest across Italy over living costs and military spending
articles.title: Thousands protest across Italy over living costs and military spending
articles.description: Thousands have protested across Italy against rising living costs and increased military spending.

articles.headline: Six-year-old girl critically injured in school assault by boy
articles.title: Six-year-old girl critically injured in alleged assault by boy at Chandigarh’s Panchkula school
articles.summary: According to police, an eight-year-old boy allegedly assaulted a six-year-old classmate inside a Panchkula classroom on October 28, 2026. The victim suffered critical injuries and was hospitalised at the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research in Chandigarh. Deputy Commissioner of Police Amrinder Singh stated that the suspect is undergoing a medical assessment to determine further legal action while authorities investigate school officials.
articles.description: The police said the eight-year-old boy is undergoing a medical assessment, while the girl remains under treatment at PGIMER, Chandigarh

articles.headline: Class 10 student seriously injured in classroom attack in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Class 10 student attacked with wood-cutting machine inside classroom in A.P.’s Anantapur; accused yet to be identified
articles.summary: A Class 10 student at Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu was seriously injured after being attacked with a wood-cutting machine inside her classroom on October 31, 2026. The unidentified accused fled the scene leaving the weapon behind, while police and state leaders including Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed authorities to apprehend the perpetrator swiftly.
articles.description: The girl who was seriously injured in the attack is undergoing treatment in a hospital; two youths who allegedly carried out the attack were not students of the school, fellow students said

articles.headline: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan warns society against accepting unverified claims
articles.title: Society that accepts unverified claims and fears questions is vulnerable to authoritarianism: Justice Bhuyan
articles.summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan stated during an address at the University of Science and Technology, Meghalaya that uncritical acceptance of claims without evidence leaves society vulnerable to authoritarianism. Speaking on October 31, 2026, he emphasized that building a scientific temper and critical inquiry among students is essential to resist misinformation and societal division.
articles.description: Speaking at the University of Science and Technology, Meghalaya, the Supreme Court judge said building a scientific temper must extend beyond laboratories to the capacity of youths and students to think rationally, and urged a shift from ‘us’ and ‘they’ to the Preamble’s ‘we’

articles.headline: Kiren Rijiju challenges Congress over electoral defeats and election commission
articles.title: Union Minister Rijiju challenges Congress to answer ‘basic questions’ amid row over SIR, CEC
articles.summary: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju challenged the Congress party on October 31, 2026, to explain its past electoral defeats while defending the special intensive revision of electoral rolls. In a post on X, he questioned Congress criticisms of the Election Commission and accused the opposition of attempting to undermine the Constitution and Indian democracy.
articles.description: Referring to the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Mr. Rijiju questioned how the Congress suffered a third consecutive defeat when Gyanesh Kumar, the incumbent Chief Election Commissioner, was not heading the poll panel

articles.headline: Isro launches NVS-03 navigation satellite to restore Navic network
articles.title: ISRO NVS-03 launch: 5 things to know about India’s new navigation satellite
articles.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation successfully launched the 2250 kg NVS-03 navigation satellite from Sriharikota on October 30, 2026, restoring the Navic system to its minimum operational configuration of four active spacecraft. The mission, featuring an indigenous atomic clock and L1 band integration, aims to provide positioning and timing services for civilian and defence applications across India and surrounding regions.
articles.description: ISRO successfully launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on October 30, 2026, restoring NavIC to a four-satellite, standalone operational status and advancing India’s push for an indigenous, more precise space-time network

articles.headline: Meitei groups hold rally in Imphal demanding chief minister resignation
articles.title: Meitei groups hold rally in Imphal; Manipur CM's resignation, abrogation of SoO truce pact sought
articles.summary: An umbrella body of Meitei groups organized a major rally in Imphal on October 31, 2026, demanding the Chief Minister's resignation and the abrogation of the Suspension of Operations agreement. COCOMI convenor Y. Dhiren criticized the government's failure to protect indigenous people amid ongoing ethnic violence that has severely affected Manipur since May 2023.
articles.description: The march came days after militants ambushed 14 Meitei men and killed three of them, sparking protests in the State

articles.headline: Texas border voters shift political allegiances amid economic and immigration pressures
articles.title: ‘Paycheck to paycheck’: Texas border voters shed parties amid economic woes
articles.summary: Voters in the Rio Grande Valley of Texas are increasingly moving away from traditional party loyalties due to economic hardships, rising freight costs, and immigration policies. Residents like Jesus Robles expressed regret over their 2024 votes as high poverty rates, inadequate infrastructure in colonias, and expensive housing continue to impact middle-class families across the region.
articles.description: Voters reassess 2024 swing towards Trump as Republicans and Democrats grapple for Rio Grande Valley votes.

articles.headline: CPCB directs Delhi-NCR authorities to close non-compliant industrial units
articles.title: CPCB threatens to shut NCR industries yet to order pollution-control devices
articles.summary: The Central Pollution Control Board directed pollution control authorities in Delhi-NCR to issue show-cause notices to industrial units failing to install air pollution control devices. Units have five days to provide evidence of equipment orders or face closure. The enforcement aims to curb winter pollution as authorities implement revised particulate matter emission norms across seventeen categories of highly polluting industries.
articles.description: In an October 30 letter, the Central Pollution Control Board asked authorities in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan to issue show-cause notices to non-compliant units under the CAQM’s revised emission norms

articles.headline: Gujarat High Court division bench stays order lifting non-veg food ban
articles.title: Gujarat HC Judge strikes down ban on non-veg food sale in Somnath; two-Judge Bench stays her order
articles.summary: A two-judge division bench of the Gujarat High Court stayed a single-judge ruling that struck down a ban on selling non-vegetarian food near the Somnath temple. Chief Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak and Justice Nirzar Desai acted on an urgent appeal from the state government, keeping the collector notification active until a hearing on December 26, 2026.
articles.description: A division Bench stayed the judgment of Justice Nisha Thakore following an urgent appeal moved by the Gujarat Government, and directed that the Collector's notification banning the sale of non-veg food will continue for now

articles.headline: Granules India facility in Hyderabad receives eleven US FDA observations
articles.title: Finished dosage facility of Granules in Hyderabad gets 11 U.S. FDA observations
articles.summary: The United States Food and Drug Administration issued eleven observations following an inspection of Granules India Limited finished dosage facility in Gagillapur, Hyderabad. Conducted from October 19 to 30, 2026, the inspection resulted in no data integrity or cross-contamination findings. The company stated that manufacturing and distribution remain unaffected and a comprehensive response will be submitted within fifteen business days.
articles.description: The U.S. FDA issued a warning letter in February 2025 after inspecting the facility in August–September 2024

articles.headline: Train crash near Urda kills 69 people and injures over 100
articles.title: Young athlete and former minister among victims of Spain train crash
articles.summary: Sixty-nine people died and more than one hundred were injured when a high-speed Renfe train collided with a stationary Iryo train near Urda on Wednesday morning. The victims of the worst rail disaster in Spain since 2013 include a twenty-four-year-old athlete and a former government minister. Forensic experts in Toledo are working to identify bodies as families provide DNA samples.
articles.description: As some of the victims' names are released publicly, an outpouring of grief and anger is sweeping across Spain.

articles.headline: Lebanese military court charges thirteen individuals over confiscated Hezbollah explosives
articles.title: Lebanon charges 13 over confiscated Hezbollah explosives
articles.summary: A Lebanese military court charged thirteen people with weapons possession, undermining state security, and forming illegal associations following the seizure of a truck carrying 780 kilograms of explosives at the Dahr al-Baydar checkpoint. Two suspects were arrested while eleven remain at large. Hezbollah acknowledged owning the shipment for use against Israel, intensifying domestic debate over the armed group disarmament.
articles.description: Group calls charges 'unjust', says weapons were meant to be used against Israeli forces in south Lebanon.

articles.headline: Kerala struggles with tourism recovery while Sri Lanka surpasses pre-pandemic arrivals
articles.title: Why Sri Lanka’s tourism is thriving amid crises while Keralam struggles to regain lost ground despite its advantages
articles.summary: Foreign tourist arrivals in Kerala continue to stagnate at roughly seventy percent of pre-pandemic figures in 2026, whereas Sri Lanka has successfully surpassed its pre-COVID visitor numbers despite sharing comparable tropical appeal and adverse global conditions. Kerala holds distinct natural advantages, including scenic backwaters and authentic Ayurveda wellness tourism, but faces ongoing momentum challenges in regaining lost ground.
articles.description: The two destinations offer comparable tourism experiences and products. Even amid adverse global conditions, Colombo has managed to surpass its pre-COVID foreign tourist arrival figures, while Keralam has struggled to regain momentum, achieving only around 70% of its pre-pandemic arrivals

articles.headline: CCTV and zip ties: How US mail-in votes are secured and counted
articles.title: CCTV and zip ties: How US mail-in votes are secured and counted

articles.headline: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado calls for elections next year
articles.title: Venezuela opposition leader María Machado calls for elections upon return
articles.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has called for national elections to be held in 2027 during a news conference in Caracas on Thursday. The Nobel Peace Prize winner dismissed interim president Delcy Rodríguez's plans for a transition as illogical. Machado returned to the country following the United States seizure of former president Nicolás Maduro and praised the Trump administration for opening the floodgate to freedom.
articles.description: Machado, who was in exile for nearly a year, said the transition in Venezuela's government would be "irreversible, organised, pacific".

articles.title: Watch: What leaked audio reveals about Spain train crash

articles.headline: Israeli forces escalate raids and displacement across West Bank
articles.title: Palestinians injured, arrested in Israeli raids across West Bank
articles.summary: Israeli military forces and settlers have intensified raids, arrests, and home demolitions across the occupied West Bank. A military offensive in the Hebron governorate has entered its seventh day, displacing thousands of residents and disrupting education for over two hundred thousand students. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs has called for an end to the forced displacements.
articles.description: This comes as more than 3,300 Palestinians are forced from homes in Hebron as Israel's military offensive continues.

articles.headline: Telangana farmers shift toward horticulture crops to combat weather challenges
articles.title: Telangana farmers’ preference for veggies, spices over paddy continues in Yasangi 2026
articles.summary: Farmers in Telangana continue cultivating vegetables and spices instead of traditional paddy during the Yasangi season due to weather impacts. State Horticulture Director Shaik Yasmeen Basha reported increased sowing areas and noted that officials are providing drought-resistant seeds and irrigation resources. District officers stated that market demand and borewell irrigation heavily drive this ongoing agricultural transition across several districts.
articles.description: Excessive heat conditions in the next few months may bring down horticulture produce by around 20%, which may drive demand, says Telangana Horticulture Department’s Director Shaik Yasmeen Basha

articles.headline: Telangana plans public-private partnership model to improve hospital MRI services
articles.title: Telangana plans PPP model to ensure uninterrupted MRI services at govt hospitals
articles.summary: The Telangana government plans to adopt a Public-Private Partnership model to operate magnetic resonance imaging services across state hospitals, aiming to resolve technical disruptions. Health Minister C. Damodara Raja Narasimha announced that scans will remain free for referred patients, following a pilot project in Mahabubnagar. Officials estimate the arrangement will reduce government expenditure by approximately twenty percent compared to existing systems.
articles.description: Health Minister C. Damodara Raja Narasimha clarified that scans will remain free of cost for patients referred by doctors at Telangana government hospitals

articles.headline: Aam Aadmi Party releases first candidate list for Punjab Assembly elections
articles.title: AAP announces first list of 40 candidates for 2027 Punjab Assembly elections
articles.summary: The Aam Aadmi Party released its first list of forty candidates for the Punjab Assembly election scheduled early next year, fielding exclusively sitting legislators. Chief Minister Bhagwall Mann confirmed his candidacy from the Dhuri constituency in Sangrur district during a press briefing on October 31, 2026. The ruling party selected candidates based on public survey responses to campaign effectively ahead of the March 16 poll.
articles.description: Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann will seek re-election from the Dhuri constituency in Sangrur district

articles.headline: Israeli elections conclude with neither political bloc winning majority
articles.title: Israel election result shows no overall majority as vote count complete
articles.summary: Vote counting is complete in Israel's parliamentary elections, leaving both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition short of the sixty-one seats required for a majority. Opposition leaders have met to explore coalition options as provisional results indicate Netanyahu's bloc secured fifty-three seats while the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot won forty-eight seats in the Knesset.
articles.description: Opposition explores options to form coalition as no party secures the 61 seats required for parliamentary majority.

articles.headline: One Planet Partners launches maiden fund to deploy over 3,000 crore rupees in India
articles.title: One Planet Partners to deploy over ₹3,000 crore in high-growth business in India
articles.summary: India-focused private equity firm One Planet Partners announced a partnership with Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank on October 29, 2026. The collaboration includes a maiden fund targeting over 3,000 crore rupees for mid-market businesses in energy, mobility, and manufacturing. Bengaluru electric mobility company Yulu serves as the first investment. The founding team includes industry veterans Mukund Rajan, Bobby Pauly, Mrinalini Mirchandani, and Sheetal Thakkar.
articles.description: The fund would focus on high-growth mid-market businesses across energy, mobility and manufacturing, with scale-up capital of ₹ 100–500 crore for enterprises with revenue between ₹200 and 2,000 crore, says One Planet Partners, an India-focused private equity firm

articles.headline: Sudan paramilitary commander Siddiq Ander defects from Rapid Support Forces
articles.title: RSF senior commander defects, accusing Sudan group’s leadership of nepotism
articles.summary: A senior commander of Sudan‘s Rapid Support Forces announced his departure in video footage published on Friday, accusing relatives of group leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo of tightly controlling finances and military promotions. The exit follows several high-profile defections this year amid an ongoing conflict between the army and the paramilitary group that has displaced millions.
articles.description: In exclusive footage obtained by Al Jazeera, Siddiq Ander describes RSF as a 'purely family-based project'.

articles.headline: Russian satellites assist Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, investigation reveals
articles.title: Are Houthis using Russian satellites as Saudi Arabia fends off strikes?
articles.summary: An investigation by Geneva-based firm AURORAH Geosignal Intelligence revealed that Russian military and reconnaissance satellites observed targeted areas before and after forty attacks against Saudi Arabia. Three officials confirmed that the Iran-aligned Houthis have benefited from Russian intelligence alongside Chinese capabilities to target energy infrastructure.
articles.description: Analysts say the seizure of state arsenals, external backing and extensive military evolution has helped the Houthis.

articles.headline: Coastal Andhra Pradesh fisherfolk face financial crisis amid weather bans
articles.title: Coastal Andhra Pradesh fisherfolk face severe financial crisis amid Cyclones and frequent weather bans
articles.summary: Marine fishing communities in coastal Andhra Pradesh are facing severe financial distress due to frequent weather warnings and compulsory fishing bans issued by the India Meteorological Department. Cumulative losses have exceeded 36 crore rupees following multiple severe weather events, prompting fisherfolk organisations to petition Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu for enhanced financial compensation.
articles.description: Repeated bans across four major weather alerts since June have caused cumulative losses exceeding ₹36 crore

articles.headline: German companies view Hyderabad as base for innovation and research
articles.title: German companies looking at Hyderabad as base for innovation, research: Consul General Michael Hasper
articles.summary: German businesses are increasingly looking at Hyderabad as a hub for technology development due to the city's pharmaceutical ecosystem, engineering talent, and global capability centres. Speaking in Hyderabad on October 30, 2026, German Consul General Michael Hasper highlighted the mutual benefits of connecting Telangana's skilled workforce with opportunities in Germany.

articles.headline: Saudi air defences intercept hostile drone in Riyadh region
articles.title: Saudi Arabia says intercepted ‘hostile drone’ in Riyadh region
articles.summary: Military coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki stated that air defences destroyed an incoming drone on October 31, 2026. articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi praises ISRO scientists for successful satellite launch
articles.title: Launch of NVS-03: PM Modi congratulates scientists, engineers at ISRO

articles.description: Mr. Modi also said that equipped with enhanced capabilities, NVS-03 will further India’s pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies and support navigation services that benefit the people

articles.headline: Donald Trump describes Brazil election as a disgrace

articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated he did not take sides in Brazil's presidential election won by Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, but described the contest as a disgrace. The remarks followed the arrival in Miami of former Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who fled Brazil with his family. The Brazilian real dropped twelve percent following the election outcome.
articles.description: Comments come after Trump ally Flavio Bolsonaro fled to Miami in US and claimed, without evidence, that vote was stolen.

articles.headline: Netanyahu attacks Palestinian-Israeli parties as he falls short of majority
articles.title: Netanyahu attacks Palestinian-Israeli parties as he falls short of majority
articles.description: With all votes now counted, opposition parties could join forces with Palestinian-Israeli parties to unseat Netanyahu.

articles.headline: K.T. Rama Rao questions Union government over proposed IDBI Bank sale
articles.title: KTR questions proposed sale of IDBI Bank, asks if its valuable real estate assets were factored in valuation
articles.summary: Bharat Rashtra Samithi working president K.T. Rama Rao questioned the Union government's proposed sale of IDBI Bank to a private entity, raising concerns regarding valuation methods, bidding norm changes, and employee grievances. In a statement on October 31, 2026, the BRS leader asked whether prime real estate assets in Hyderabad were factored into the valuation and questioned the urgency behind the privatization of the public sector bank.
articles.description: BRS working president sought to know why the concerns raised by IDBI Bank employees over the proposed disinvestment were not being addressed

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu Congress and VCK mobilise cadres for New Delhi protest
articles.title: Tamil Nadu Congress, VCK mobilise cadres for Nov. 1 INDIA bloc protest in New Delhi
articles.summary: Demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi have activated party networks to mobilise cadres for an INDIA bloc protest in New Delhi on November 1, 2026. According to Mayiladuthurai Member of Parliament R. Sudha, the Indian National Congress expects over five lakh participants, while alleging that the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Centre is curtailing parliamentary privileges.
articles.description: “We expect more than five lakh Congress cadres to participate. From Tamil Nadu, we are expecting at least 100 party workers to reach New Delhi from each district,” says MP R. Sudha

articles.headline: Authorities resume operations to recover chopper crash victims in Uttarakhand
articles.title: Operation underway to recover bodies from remote chopper crash site in Uttarakhand
articles.summary: Rescue operations resumed on October 31, 2026, to recover the bodies of six victims from a helicopter crash in Joshimath, Uttarakhand. The Trans Bharat Aviation private helicopter was returning from Badrinath when it crashed, killing the pilot and five pilgrims from Karnataka. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami stated that an investigation into the cause is underway by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau.
articles.description: A team from the forest department, Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau officials, a DGCA team have all been dispatched to the crash site

articles.headline: Karnataka places three-year moratorium on new private PU colleges
articles.title: Karnataka places three-year moratorium on permission for new private PU colleges
articles.summary: To regulate pre-university education, the Karnataka government has proposed a three-year moratorium on new private PU colleges for the 2027 to 2030 academic years. The draft rules follow data showing available seats outpace passing students, leaving thousands vacant. The Karnataka State Pre-University Colleges Lecturers Association welcomed the move while calling for improved government college infrastructure.
articles.description: The decision to restrict opening of new colleges comes in the backdrop of the number of seats available in I PU increasing every year, outpacing the number of students passing SSLC exams

articles.headline: Kerala Crime Branch registers FIR against KPSC chairperson and members
